Breaking: Como, Milla stende l'AEK. Fabregas vede i playoff di Champions: "Non è normale"

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (333 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Tuttomercatoweb

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that non è stata una passeggiata di salute.
  • According to recent reports, "Per il Como non è normale fare 8 vittorie su 9", ha esordito l'allenatore del Como, Cesc Fabregas in conferenza stampa post-partita.
  • Marko Nikolic, tecnico dell'AEK Atene, "Per me è una delle squadre più forti in Europa.

Recent findings suggest that non è stata una passeggiata di salute. Sotto la pioggia copiosa del Sinigaglia, il Como ha conquistato la sua quarta vittoria della Champions League ed è a un passo dall'aritmetica qualificazione tra le prime 24 forze d'Europa. Un rigore sbagliato da Da Cunha, il doppio salvataggio di Robert Sanchez al termine del primo tempo, mentre il gioiello di Luis Milla all'incrocio dei pali ha deciso l'incontro 1-0. Il Como vince e vede la qualificazione ai playoff.

According to recent reports, "Per il Como non è normale fare 8 vittorie su 9", ha esordito l'allenatore del Como, Cesc Fabregas in conferenza stampa post-partita. Soffermandosi ad ampio spettro sui risultati ottenuti finora lungo il cammino del club lariano da quando il catalano ha in mano le redini della squadra: "Sappiamo che è un progetto speciale. Sono il primo che celebra 5 minuti e poi andiamo alla prossima. Ma se torniamo a tre anni fa, è vero, siamo cresciuti velocemente. Dobbiamo godercela almeno un attimo. Viviamo in un mondo che se perdi con il Frosinone ti ammazzano. Bisogna capire quello che sta succedendo, con umiltà e la voglia di lavorare. Si sta facendo una cosa diversa e speciale. All'esterno sembra una normalità. Quando sono arrivato quattro anni e mezzo fa, io ad allenare tre anni fa. Lo valorizziamo, piano piano, per ritrovare le forze. Voi scriverete che siamo meglio della Juventus, ma è la squadra più storica d'Italia. Noi dobbiamo trovare la forza per fare la partita perfetta un'altra volta".

Marko Nikolic, tecnico dell'AEK Atene, "Per me è una delle squadre più forti in Europa. Complimenti al suo allenatore, sapevamo fosse difficile giocare con il Como. Ha fatto 4 gol con il Manchester United e capite che è difficile giocare contro una squadra così. Hanno uno straordinario arsenale offensivo, ma sono contento per come abbiamo affrontato la partita. Avremmo potuto perderla però in altri modi, non con questo errore. Pazienza. Comunque era una squadra molto giovane e interessante".

Xabi Alonso hits out at ‘soft’ Chelsea players

📅 12 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 23 min read (4626 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~23 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Xabi Alonso accused his Chelsea players of being “soft” after they failed to keep a clean sheet for the 20th successive Premier League game.
  • Chelsea threw away an early lead to draw 2-2 with Hull City and have conceded two or more goals in each of their four Premier League games.
  • Alonso has tried different systems and different players in those games, but suggested Chelsea’s biggest problem is mental.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Xabi Alonso accused his Chelsea players of being “soft” after they failed to keep a clean sheet for the 20th successive Premier League game.

Chelsea threw away an early lead to draw 2-2 with Hull City and have conceded two or more goals in each of their four Premier League games.

Alonso has tried different systems and different players in those games, but suggested Chelsea’s biggest problem is mental.

The club’s dreadful clean-sheet record pre-dates him and is the first time in 65 years Chelsea have gone 20 league games without keeping the opposition out.

Hull’s first goal from Mohamed Belloumi came after the ball had bounced over Jorrel Hato and Alonso remarked: “We need to be aware that from any situation, any team in the Premier League can hurt you. Today it was from a long ball, two bounces, the way it happened. You need to be very aware, very ready that the danger can come from any situation. If you are soft or if you are not prepared, you will get punished and we have been punished that way.”.

Chelsea have shared 30 goals with their opponents in the club’s six games in all competitions so far this season.

“Yeah, it’s all maybe entertaining, but I hope that one day you say it was a boring game and we win and we don’t give these entertaining moments,” he said.

Industry observers note that “But, for sure, it kind of repeats some patterns that we are making. It will take time to... or it will take moments to fix them when we get the lead and you still need to be competing and not give the chance so easily for them to come back, especially in the first goal, we can do much better.

“It was too soft to give them this hope because until then we were controlling, we were creating chances. But that momentum that we had changed the mood and the score of the game, and it’s something that we need to be talking [about], we address and we will get better. But it’s having an impact on our performances at the moment.”.

Asked if his players have a real desire to defend and keep clean sheets, Alonso stated: “We can do better, we can do better for sure. We need to know that even when we have the lead, a very notable part of the game is to hold together, to keep the distance, to go intense in the situations to defend. I’m sure that we can do better.

“Overall, I think that we are attacking better than defending in every part. We know that it’s a massive topic and a big theme for us. For sure, it’s just four games. But the dynamic in terms of conceding, I don’t like it and we need to do much better. Open play, set-pieces, long balls, this toughness, this competitive sense, we can do better.”.

Needing three goals or more to win games is not sustainable, as Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso is finding out.

This is not a problem of Alonso’s making, given Chelsea have now gone 20 Premier League games without a clean sheet. But he is certainly not improving the concern yet.

Chelsea beat Fulham with three goals and Brighton with four but left themselves far too much to do against Arsenal and were taken advantage of by Hull City, who will be slightly disappointed they did not leave Stamford Bridge with all three points.

Goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez has now conceded seven goals in three games since joining from Aston Villa, while central defender Maxence Lacroix, who joined for £52m from Crystal Palace in the summer, was relegated to the substitutes’ bench.

Martínez was at fault for Mohamed Belloumi’s second goal, but the Argentine did make a crucial save at his back post to stop substitute Mohamed-Ali Cho grabbing a winner that Chelsea could have had no complaints about.

It has been revealed that hull finished the game with more shots on goal than their hosts and a higher expected-goals rate. Chelsea are far too open and in some ways far too entertaining.

Defensive midfielder Moisés Caicedo cannot return from injury swiftly enough, but this does not feel like a problem that will be solved by one man. Alonso needs to find a balance and instil a real desire in his team to defend.

Caicedo has that desire, but there are no defenders at the club who have shown that absolute desperation to keep the ball out of the net that Chelsea fans became so used to in the days of John Terry, Gary Cahill and César Azpilicueta.

None of this should diminish Hull’s performance. They were not only spirited and full of character but also demonstrated quality and a threat. The joke is currently on those who laughed at their hopes of survival before a ball had been kicked.

According to recent reports, it is now two wins and two draws for Sergej Jakirovic’s team and they are already a fifth of the way to 40 points. Jakirovic had promised his staff a week off in the international break if they reached eight points after five games. With that target already met, there may be a newly introduced reward if Hull can make it 11 points against Newcastle United next weekend.

“Before the season, I noted to my staff that we will take seven, eight points in these first five and then I will give them seven days off,” Jakirovic said. “That was our target and now we are in a very good position, eight points.

Recent findings suggest that “Especially today, it’s very, very difficult to play here, and now we will try to get even more. Of course, I’m a little bit worried about the international break because we have 13 national team players. But we will see who will come back and in what condition. So this is my concern right now.” Asked if his staff’s seven-day break will be extended if Hull can beat Newcastle, Jakirovic added: “I will tell them. But I know already.”.

While his five-game target may need modifying, Jakirovic is not deviating from his goal for the season for Hull. “Our target is always to stay in the league and collect as many points as possible,” he mentioned. “Forty points, 38 to 41, this is the average we need. Then it’s easier to play. You can play more relaxed, with more joy and happiness. So [get to] this as soon as possible, so that we are safe.”.

Hull had not conceded a league goal before this and there had been predictions they might crumble when they finally let the ball into their net. They did so after just seven minutes but they kept their heads and came back stronger.

It was far too easy for Morgan Rogers to make a yard of space for himself to shoot after collecting the ball from João Pedro, and Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis may not have been happy to have been beaten at his near post.

Chelsea have now scored inside the first 10 minutes in all of their four league games, but Hull were in no mood to crumble and hit back with two goals in six minutes from Belloumi to take a half-time lead. Both Hull goals were shockers from Chelsea’s perspective. The first, in the 28th minute, came as a result of Jorrel Hato letting the ball bounce over him from a Ryan Giles cross and Belloumi finished brilliantly.

Sources indicate that belloumi’s second came after Martínez had flapped at a corner and Semi Ajayi had hit the bar with a header. The ball fell to Belloumi again and his shot was deflected into the net.

Recent findings suggest that it was no surprise that Hato did not reappear for the second half, as he was replaced by Pep Chavarría at left-back. But Chelsea remained vulnerable and Martínez had to recover from spilling a Regan Slater shot to prevent Ollie McBurnie extending Hull’s advantage.

When Palmer and Pedro combined for Pedro to sweep the ball into the net and equalise with 24 minutes remaining, it seemed like it would be Chelsea who would provide the grandstand finish.

But it was Hull who got a second wind and Chelsea were indebted to Martínez for making a save to stop Cho securing all three points and sending the visiting fans home even happier.

I feel good. We have to be happy. It’s a huge result for us.

In a recent development, we had 2-1 at half-time and we had a 100 per cent chance with McBurnie but Martinez’s save was excellent. We have to control play better in the box because we can stop this [Chelsea goal]. We had an excellent chance for Cho – Martinez saved again. Player of the match.

Industry observers note that we can be very happy. We took a point in a very demanding match.

In a recent development, eight points against very difficult opponents. We have to continue like this.

According to recent reports, there have been 12 Premier League games at Anfield in 2026, Liverpool have only won 4 of them to date. This was seventh draw and Fulham deserves their share of the spoils. This was very much a learning experience for Andoni Iraola.

Not a single home win in the Premier League, today.

Aston Villa 1 Nottingham Forest 2Bournemouth 2 Brentford 2Chelsea 2 Hull City 2Crystal Palace 2 Ipswich Town 3Liverpool 0 Fulham 0.

What a result for Hull, who remain unbeaten and they have taken five points from fixtures against United, Villa and Chelsea.

That is the first really poor result of the Alonso era, points dropped.

What a thriller in SE25, both teams have been going for it in the closing stages, but Ipswich have surely score the winner through Zian Flemming.

It has been revealed that fulham were pointless before this game, but they have kept a clean sheet at Anfield with a disciplined display and they could well have score one or two. Underwhelming for Liverpool, who have not won just one of their first four games and their fixtures have not been the most taxing.

And as we predicted at the beginning of the game... Liverpool 0 Fulham 0. If this reporter ever gives you advice on a horse to back or a team to follow, make sure you take the opposite stance. Fulham deserve their reward and their fans are singing “We got a point!”.

Villa are finishing the game with 10 men because Ian Maatsen pulled up after Emery had made his five substitutions, and Forest have punished them through Igor Jesus with just a few minutes of normal time to play.

In a recent development, alexander Isak heads over the bar when he perhaps should have hit the target. Has time run out for Liverpool?

You might imagine Chelsea are battering down the door, but Mohamed-Ali Cho has just forced Emi Martinez into a save at the other end. Hull will remain unbeaten if they can hold out.

Strand Larsen has had his critics, but he has scored his first goal of the season to set up a grandstand finish with 15 minutes plus stoppage time to play at Selhurst Park.

Short corner, McGinn whipped in an inswinging cross that is glanced into the bottom corner by Alysson.

Liverpool continue to toil at Anfield, but no opening goal. Iraola has thrown on Frimpong, Mac Allister, Ngumoha and Gakpo in the second half. Fulham have had the chances to score at least one, and Josh King has just brought a save out of Alisson.

Hull are a little lucky they still have 11 men on the pitch. Already on a booking, my man Crooks bundled down Rogers. It could easily have been another yellow car but the referee let him off and now he’s been replaced by Iroegbunam.

Joao Pedro finds the smallest of gaps to be the goalkeeper and find the roof of the net with a brilliant, instinctive finish.

According to recent reports, that had not really been coming for Chelsea. It all felt a bit easy for Palmer to get his low cross into the box and Pedro to sweep the ball in. The home fans have woken up again.

In a recent development, martinez was lucky to get away with another slip up, there. He spilt Slater’s shot but reacted before McBurnie to stop the Hull striker scoring the rebound. Just a day after his nasty looking crash, Sorba Thomas is on for Hull.

It has been revealed that this game is absolutely here for Fulham to win. Quietness has descended around Anfield, the hosts have no fluency in their play and Fulham are growing in confidence. Why wouldn’t they after getting to 65 minutes with a clean sheet?

Recent findings suggest that just like in the first half, four minutes after one of these teams taking the lead there has been an equaliser. Kevin Scahde is in a rich vein of form.

In a recent development, bournemouth have have never beaten Brentford in the Premier League, but they might well be on their way to changing that record having trailed earlier in the game. Marcus Tavernier has just scored their second goal.

Sources indicate that matt Davidson Rider Crooks has just been booked for a very cynical foul on Rogers. It gave Chelsea a free-kick in a dangerous position Reece James had an effort tipped away. Chelsea have started the second half well.

Within a minute of the restart, Villa lose the ball in midfield and Delap punishes them to the maximum. Cracking finish from just outside the box, and a much-needed goal by Delap. The Glasner curse striking for Emery again?

Liam Delap has just started paying back that £50m transfer fee with a fine goal.

Delap picked the ball up on the left and set himself up on the edge of the box before crashing a 25-yard shot past Zion Suzuki.

Unai Emery has made a couple of changes at half-time, taking off Nicolas Jackson who picked up a silly booking just before half-time.

Tammy Abraham is on in his place. George Hemmings is also off and replaced by Alysson.

Industry observers note that pep Chavarria on for Chelsea at half-time. He’s replaced Jorrel Hato, who had a bit of a stinker in the first half.

Andoni Iraola hasn’t hung about here. Milos Kerkez has come on immediately after half-time for Kostas Tsimikas and you can say with certainty that Liverpool will be shopping for a new left-back in due course.

So at half-time, Hull City are top of the Premier League and don’t their supporters know it? They were singing “we are top of the League” for the full two minutes of time added on for stoppages at the end of the first period. Alonso has some work to do at the break.

Forest did need a brilliant double save from Matz Sels to deny Victor Lindelof and have recovered to slow the match down.

Neco Williams wasted a decent chance for Forest from outside the penalty area shortly before the break.

Referee Andrew Madley has irritated both teams with a number of weird decisions - but that’s sadly par for the course with officials nowadays.

Villa 0 Forest 0Bournemouth 1 Brentford 1Chelsea 1 Hull City 2Palace 1 Ipswich 2Liverpool 0 Fulham 0.

Palace in some trouble now, level with Ipswich and down to 10 men. Disasi was sent off in the 34th minute for a reckless challenge on Jack Clarke, caught him with studs on shin.

Things got worse for Palace just before half-time, with Leif Davis heading home at the back post to give Ipswich the league.

Recent findings suggest that apologies for the lack of updates, some technical gremlins at Telegraph Towers. A nip and tuck game as expected at at the Vitality: Kevin Schade gave Brentford the lead before Justin Kluivert equalised four minutes later.

In a recent development, one way to put it is that Kostas Tsimikas isn’t playing well. Another way to say it would be that his efforts are making Milos Kerkez look like Roberto Carlos. The Greek left-back is having a dreadful afternoon and Fulham are getting plenty of joy out of him. We suggested there was no chance of this game finishing goalless, and it’s anomalous that we have reached 40 minutes without score. Fulham, certainly, have a sense of adventure and have been into Liverpool’s 18-yard box plenty of times. Let’s see if the picture changes before the interval.

That’s now seven goals Emi Martinez has conceded in three games since joining from Villa to supposedly solve Chelsea’s goalkeeping crisis. Martinez won’t be pleased with Hull’s second goal, here. He was beaten to a corner by Ajayi. His header hit the bar and Belloumi’s shot was deflected past him. The Hull fans are in dreamland.

Recent findings suggest that “Ciao! Dovresti venire qualche giorno qui a Creta. Alla Elounda Hotel c’è la Penthouse Spa, dove ti puoi rigenerare con la SIX SENSES SPA. Incredibili massaggi fusion, con programmi olistici e ayurvedici”.

Recent findings suggest that ho ricevuto questa telefonata da un’amica, mentre andavo a mangiare nel solito ristorante, con TV, davanti al CityLife. Mi è venuto da sorridere.

“Non cambierei nessun massaggio rilassante all’alga marina e agli estratti di passiflora con l’esperienza vissuta oggi a San Siro!”, rispondo convinto.

“Ah, sei stato in una delle dieci piscine delle nuove Terme De Montel, davanti allo stadio? Sono bravissimi nell’applicazione di Savon Beldi, il sapone nero, nell’Hammam, il bagno turco!”.

Recent findings suggest that “No, cara, non hai capito. Non sono stato davanti a San Siro. Sono andato dentro San Siro, dove ho passato cento minuti di assoluto relax. I tuoi impacchi di argilla non erano nulla rispetto a quello che ho provato, grazie alle prodezze dei giocatori del Milan. Ha cominciato Modric, con un lancio a Rabiot, idratante come olio di jojoba. Poi si è presentato Rabiot con giocate e fughe, delicate come un mix di Achillea Millefoglie blu, Vetiver e Patchouli. Mi è venuta la pelle liscia come quella di un bimbo, quando Diego Moreira toccava il pallone. Sembrava mi spalmassi una crema Ylang Ylang. E Pulisic, Ramos, Jashari, rigeneranti come Olio Mosqueta? Siamo usciti dallo stadio più freschi, più belli, più sereni, anche se non avevamo davanti il mare di Creta”.

La mia amica non ha risposto. Ha chiuso la comunicazione, forse un po’ scioccata, ma certamente con un tocco di invidia per non avere trascorso un bel pomeriggio di calcio.

È stato bravo Amorim a studiare pregi e difetti del Frosinone, squadra intensa e coraggiosa, che Alvini ha voluto presentare contro il Milan senza rinnegare i principi di gioco, fondamentali per la conquista dei meritati venti punti. Unica colpa, forse, del tecnico portoghese quella di non sostituire, a venti minuti dalla fine, Modric e Rabiot. Mentre il francese ha chiuso senza problemi fisici, il fuoriclasse croato, nei minuti finali, ha accusato un fastidio a un muscolo, che lo costringerà a dare forfait ad Atene e Cagliari. Jashari, la sua alternativa, ha offerto un'eccellente prestazione domenica, ma il suo rendimento non è mai stato ottimale, in questa stagione, quando ha giocato senza avere accanto Modric. Ad Atene deve smentire questa sensazione, anzi questa realtà. Atene, la città delle due Champions League, quella di Capello e quella di Ancelotti. Anche Amorim spera di ripetere le vittorie dei suoi celebri colleghi sotto il Partenone, perché, in futuro, anche lui possa sempre esclamare:.

“DOPO FERENCVAROS C’È SEMPRE ATENE!”.

Europe's biggest surprise package: Frosinone's remarkable rise as the newly introduced Roberto De Zerbi takes Italian minnows owned by Ipswich chiefs to within reach of Europe after eight promotions

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 02:00 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 05:49 EST, 21 November 2026.
  • Sources indicate that not quite 50 miles south of Rome sits Frosinone.
  • Frosinone are sixth in Serie A after a flying start to their first season, at the moment above Juventus and Napoli in the table.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By FABRIZIO FERRARI FOR DAILY MAIL SPORT.

Published: 02:00 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 05:49 EST, 21 November 2026.

Sources indicate that not quite 50 miles south of Rome sits Frosinone. It is a town of 42,000 best known for many years as the birthplace of 20th-century screen icon Marcello Mastroianni and global hotelier Carmine Forte, but now the talk of Italian football.

Frosinone are sixth in Serie A after a flying start to their first season, at the moment above Juventus and Napoli in the table.

Armed with the second-lowest budget in the league, they have regularly started with seven Italian players – the most in the league – including Antonio Raimondo, a 22-year-old striker on loan from Bologna, who scored nine goals in 10 appearances before being halted by injury at the start of this month.

The majority owner is Latest York investment fund Clara Vista, who are part of the consortium behind Ipswich Town, and the head coach is Massimiliano Alvini, who has drawn comparisons to Roberto De Zerbi for both the high-intensity elements of his style and his rise from the humble depths of Italian football.

Only 18 months ago, in May 2025, they looked set to slide into the third tier, bound for a relegation play-off until Brescia were deducted points to hand Frosinone an unlikely stay of execution.

A month later a fresh sporting director, Renzo Castagnini, arrived and installed Alvini, who kept faith in most of the squad that had survived only by the skin of its teeth. Survival was again the sole aim. Yet from the very first Coppa Italia fixture Frosinone began to turn heads, beating Monza, a team widely tipped for promotion.

By the end of the season, they had finished as runners-up behind Venezia and above Monza who were promoted via the play-offs. It was Frosinone’s fourth promotion to Serie A and by far the most beautiful because nobody saw it coming.

Massimiliano Alvini was recognised as the best coach of Serie B at the 35th edition of the FIGC Panchina D'Oro Awards on Monday.

Frosinone Calcio players celebrated their victory against Lecce in October.

Much of the credit belongs to Alvini, who was named by his fellow managers on Monday as Serie B’s best coach for 2025-26. The 56-year-old Tuscan played at an amateur level until a serious injury forced him to quit at 30. His coaching career began in the same lowly ranks for Italian football.

He and his brother Walter sold shoe soles for a living. Increasingly, Walter would be asked to cover at work as his brother followed his new passion, travelling to study the training sessions of established coaches, including Luciano Spalletti at Roma and Maurizio Sarri at Empoli.

Alvini remains grounded and stubbornly modest despite eight promotions and the sudden spotlight.

If the season ended today, Frosinone would qualify for Europe but perhaps the most incredible part of the story was improvements made last season by individual players who had barely registered in the previous season.

It has been revealed that notably Fares Ghedjemis, who went from scoring two goals to 15. Also Castagnini signings such as Giacomo Calo and others including Giorgi Kvernadze, Gabriele Bracaglia and goalkeeper Lorenzo Palmisani.

Frosinone won 3-0 at Fiorentina, beat Cesc Fabregas’s Como 2-0 and Torino by the same score. At Atalanta – the Europa League winners of 2024 now managed by Sarri – they drew 4-4 and came within a whisker of a late winner.

Twenty points from the first ten games recalled the early bursts of Claudio Ranieri’s newly promoted Fiorentina in 1994-95 and Juventus in 2007-08.

Recent findings suggest that then, in the last fixture before the international break, came a third defeat of the season, at home against Cagliari, despite 29 shots and 13 corners. One of those days when the ball simply refused to go in.

Whether the shareholders of Clara Vista – which bought 80 per cent of Frosinone in the summer – are entirely delighted remains to be seen. There have been suggestions they hoped to see more of the 13 players signed via their data algorithms but only Patrizio Masini and Romano Schmid have been regular starters.

The other nine or 10 names regularly in the starting XI are the same men who drove the climb out of Serie B.

Defensive midfielder Giacomo Calo has scored five goals in 11 games this season.

Sources indicate that when it comes to the metric of ‘passes per defensive action’, a key indicator of how rapidly the ball is won back, Frosinone rank among the top four clubs in Europe. The others are Barcelona, Brighton and De Zerbi’s Tottenham.

Still, Alvini shrugs off the praise. His first seven years as a coach produced two promotions, one sacking and one relegation. Then a group of friends decided to start a club in the seventh tier (the third amateur level) and put him in charge.

In the seven seasons from 2008 to 2015, Tuttocuoio climbed via four promotions into Serie C.

Alvini moved on to fresh challenges. The next four seasons at Pistoiese and AlbinoLeffe brought his first two professional sackings. He lists them openly on LinkedIn, almost as badges of honour, albeit the second was not a conventional dismissal.

Emergency surgery to insert an artery stent early in the season left him psychologically raw when he returned.

According to recent reports, those three years at AlbinoLeffe however proved formative because he was able to watch Gian Piero Gasperini’s Atalanta methods at close quarters. He took that inspiration into the following campaign at Reggiana, taking them back to Serie B after 21 years for his seventh promotion.

Recent findings suggest that frosinone supplied the eighth and his second taste of Serie A. The first came when he was tempted from Perguia to Cremonese with a team simply not equipped for a relegation scrap. He was sacked by January.

The return is proving sweeter than he could have dared to imagine.

Col City il miglior Napoli della stagione. E Allegri assicura: "De Bruyne resta fino a giugno"

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, il Napoli torna da Manchester con un punto, qualche rimpianto e soprattutto tante certezze in più.
  • Nel post-partita, ai microfoni di Sky Sport, Allegri ha sottolineato i progressi della squadra, soprattutto nella gestione delle due fasi: “I ragazzi sono stati bravi nell'uscita palla, tecnicamente abbiamo fatto buone cose e soprattutto bene nel non possesso nel rallentare l'azione del City.
  • Di tutt'altro tenore l'analisi di Enzo Maresca, che ha riconosciuto le difficoltà difensive della propria squadra e i meriti dell'organizzazione tattica del Napoli: “Il problema difensivo è abbastanza chiaro e dobbiamo risolverlo.

In a recent development, il Napoli torna da Manchester con un punto, qualche rimpianto e soprattutto tante certezze in più. La squadra di Massimiliano Allegri pareggia per 2-2 all'Etihad Stadium contro il Manchester City, al termine di una prova collettiva di grande spessore. Gli azzurri soffrono senza mai disunirsi, limitano le occasioni degli inglesi e sfiorano il vantaggio già nel primo tempo con Beukema, fermato da un ottimo Donnarumma. Nella ripresa Hojlund sblocca il risultato con un diagonale preciso su assist di Gilmour, prima del pareggio firmato da Bouaddi. Nel momento di maggiore difficoltà, Noa Lang riporta avanti il Napoli con uno splendido destro al volo su cross di Spinazzola, ma una prodezza individuale di Cherki all'86' fissa il risultato sul definitivo 2-2. Gli azzurri salgono a quattro punti dopo cinque giornate di Champions League, mentre i Citizens raggiungono quota dieci. Al di là delle implicazioni in termini di classifica, la notizia migliore per Allegri è la risposta della squadra, arrivata peraltro in piena emergenza.

Nel post-partita, ai microfoni di Sky Sport, Allegri ha sottolineato i progressi della squadra, soprattutto nella gestione delle due fasi: “I ragazzi sono stati bravi nell'uscita palla, tecnicamente abbiamo fatto buone cose e soprattutto bene nel non possesso nel rallentare l'azione del City. Ci deve essere l'amaro in bocca per la mancata vittoria anche se il pareggio è il risultato più giusto”. Il tecnico si è assunto anche parte delle responsabilità per le precedenti difficoltà difensive, evidenziando il cambio di atteggiamento visto a Manchester: “Stasera loro per far gol hanno dovuto sudare e questo è l'atteggiamento giusto per vincere le partite”. Tra i temi più importanti della serata, però, c'è anche il futuro di Kevin De Bruyne. Il belga ha ricevuto una standing ovation dal pubblico dell'Etihad al momento della sostituzione, prima di abbracciare Allegri a bordocampo. L'allenatore ha poi allontanato le voci di un possibile addio a gennaio, esprimendo fiducia sulla permanenza del centrocampista: “Ne parlerà con la società. Kevin è un ragazzo serio e credo che rimarrà fino a giugno”. Una presa di posizione che fa seguito alle dichiarazioni del direttore sportivo Giovanni Manna, che nel prepartita aveva ricordato come il belga fosse sotto contratto fino al termine della stagione, con un'opzione per il rinnovo.

Di tutt'altro tenore l'analisi di Enzo Maresca, che ha riconosciuto le difficoltà difensive della propria squadra e i meriti dell'organizzazione tattica del Napoli: “Il problema difensivo è abbastanza chiaro e dobbiamo risolverlo. Per il resto sono abbastanza sereno, sempre difficile attaccare un blocco basso come quello del Napoli”. L'allenatore italiano ha spiegato anche le ragioni delle proprie scelte iniziali, riconoscendo come l'ingresso degli esterni offensivi abbia permesso ai Citizens di creare maggiori pericoli. Maresca ha poi invitato ad avere pazienza per il nuovo corso del Manchester City dopo un decennio trascorso sotto la guida di Pep Guardiola: “Ci vuole un po' di tempo, ma in generale sono contento”. La priorità resta quella di trovare il giusto compromesso tra la produzione offensiva e la solidità difensiva. Il Napoli, invece, può tornare a concentrarsi sul campionato con rinnovato entusiasmo: domenica c'è il Sassuolo, un appuntamento che Allegri ha già indicato come particolarmente delicato sotto il profilo mentale.

Muller: “Inter come il Bayern, tutti danno qualcosa in più. Ma lo Stoccarda può sorprendere”

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Scegli Fcinter1908.it come tuo sito preferito su Google: clicca qui.

Intervistato da La Gazzetta dello Sport, il doppio ex di Inter e Stoccarda Hansi Muller ha parlato della sfida di domani sera a San Siro:.

«Non vedo l’ora di tornare a Milano, a San Siro, anche per tirare fuori poi il mio dialetto milanese. L’Italia mi ha migliorato come persona, mi ha arricchito con amicizie profonde, sempre attive».

Industry observers note that lei è stato il primo nei quattro trasferimenti diretti tra Stoccarda e Inter. Poi sono arrivati Klinsmann, Sammer e Kuzmanovic. Come è stato scoperto?

«Dovevo venire già dopo che abbiamo vinto gli Europei nell’80. Avevo 23 anni, pensavo che fosse troppo presto. Sandro Mazzola e il ds Giancarlo Beltrami vennero a Monaco per una partita della Germania contro l’Austria: abbiamo vinto 1-0, avevo segnato e il gol è stato anche eletto il migliore del mese. Ho spiegato la mia idea e loro virarono su Herbert Prohaska».

According to recent reports, «No, e due anni dopo, l’austriaco è andato alla Roma: loro si sono ripresentati. Beltrami mi ha portato un modellino di San Siro in miniatura, con una base di marmo, lo stadio bellissimo, con lo stemma dell’Inter. L’ha tirato fuori da una tasca, non era più grande come un cellulare. Mi disse: “In questo stadio tu puoi giocare”. Non ho mai dimenticato quel momento. E quella riproduzione del Meazza l’ho donata al museo del calcio tedesco di Dortmund. Resterà sempre lì, come ricordo».

Cosa significava l’Inter a quei tempi?

According to recent reports, «Tre aspetti: primo, aveva sempre un grande nome. Juve, Milan e Inter erano sempre molto attraenti. Secondo è chiaro che potevi guadagnare di più, un argomento che aiuta nel cambiare la società o andare all’estero. Però la terza cosa, vista anche oggi, è per me la più importante: vivere in un altro paese, in un posto eccezionale come l’Italia, imparare la lingua, adattarsi a questo ambiente, alla cultura, a un modo di vivere ti fa crescere. Oggi a 69 anni sono convinto che quello che vale di più è la persona, è l’uomo, e non la coppa che hai in vetrina. Chiaro che vuoi vincere dei titoli quando giochi, ma contano di più le persone. Dopo oltre 40 anni ho ancora amici e contatti frequenti con l’Italia. Nei giorni scorsi mi sono sentito con Fulvio Collovati, quando ho visto Bergomi al funerale di Brehme ci siamo abbracciati come due fratelli. Vuol dire che ho lasciato un buon ricordo».

E la nostra lingua non l’ha mai dimenticata.

According to recent reports, «Già. Ho anche approfittato del fatto che c’erano solo due stranieri, allora dovevi imparare per forza l’italiano. E i primi sei mesi sono stato solo a Milano, mia moglie non poteva licenziarsi dalla Mercedes e mi ha raggiunto solo a Natale. Mi ha sentito parlare al telefono un quarto d’ora con dei vostri colleghi ed era stupita. “Cosa sta succedendo? Ma come parli? Incredibile”».

Veniamo all’Inter di oggi: anche con l’Atalanta si è mostrata una squadra a due facce, come i suoi risultati stagionali. Spiegazioni?

Sources indicate that «Negli ultimi anni è sempre in cima, tra scudetti e finali di Champions. Per gli avversari è sempre una partita molto attraente, importante, mettono qualche “percento” in più per fare bella figura contro l’Inter. Tu quindi devi essere sempre al 100%, ma è difficile presentarsi sempre perfetto. Se ti manca solo il 5% gli altri ne approfittano. L’Inter è un po’ come il Bayern. È la numero uno, e tutti gli altri danno di più, quando la incontrano, è una partita fuori dal normale. Se sei sotto tono rischi, si è visto in questa stagione».

Lo Stoccarda invece che squadra è? Ha un punto in più dell’Inter in Champions.

It has been revealed that «Noi diciamo wundertüte , il sacchetto delle sorprese, non sai cosa trovi. Non ha una sola faccia. Però l’Inter non deve sottovalutarla. Se i suoi osservatori hanno visto la prima mezzora con l’Atletico, non succederà. Gli spagnoli avranno pensato, “vabbè è solo lo Stoccarda”, e sono stati dominati all’inizio. Poi è finita 1-1, ma per mezzora i nostri avevano un’occasione ogni due minuti. L’Inter non li prenderà sotto gamba se ha analizzato questa partita. Era una mia piccola speranza, però sono sicuro che non succederà più».

Quali sono le caratteristiche dello Stoccarda?

Sources indicate that «Sebastian Hoeness è un bravo allenatore e ha il vantaggio di confrontarsi quasi tutti i giorni con il padre Dieter, ex grande centravanti e manager. Se tu hai come consigliere una leggenda che è anche tuo padre, lui vuole il meglio per te, ti dice le cose come stanno. Tutto lo staff è giovane, quindi più vicino all’età della rosa. Sanno come funzionano alcuni meccanismi mentali dei giocatori. Loro fanno dei capolavori. C’è molto affiatamento, e poi un altro aspetto».

In a recent development, «È una squadra con molti mancini. Anche quattro o cinque possono essere titolari. E parlo da mancino, noi siamo meno prevedibili, un po’ come nel tennis. Se ce ne sono tanti, possono causare difficoltà agli avversari. Sto parlando di Chabot, Hendriks, Mittelstädt, Stiller, Spalt. Con loro è un altro gioco».

Vi siete accorti anche in Germania di Pio Esposito?

«Sì, ragazzo eccezionale, visto anche in Nazionale, sta facendo grandi cose».

Dopo lo Stoccarda per l’Inter ci sarà il Borussia Dortmund, attuale capolista della Bundesliga. Sarà un ostacolo più duro?

«Il Borussia Dortmund non è migliore dello Stoccarda. Sono primi in Bundesliga, però con noi hanno vinto con molta fortuna, non è al livello del Bayern».

Industry observers note that umberto Chiariello, giornalista, ha commentato a Canale 21 il pari del Napoli con il Manchester City in Champions League: “Migliore in campo Allegri, tre spanne sopra tutti. Perché ci ha sorpreso tutti, con uno schieramento che nessuno aveva immaginato, prima mettendo in campo Lang, che era dato in panchina, ma soprattutto spostando Spinazzola a destra e giocando con il 4-3-3, con De Bruyne mezzala, che è il suo ruolo, numero 8, sacrificando Anguissa e facendolo entrare nel momento opportuno, quando la pressione era insostenibile e De Bruyne non ne aveva proprio più. Stasera due non mi hanno soddisfatto, De Bruyne e Milinkovic-Savic Perché De Bruyne ha avuto due palle al 57° e al 67°, me le sono appuntate, dove è solo a palla, Hojlund gli detta la profondità, uno come lui lo deve mandare in porta alla squadra, non per fare il lavoro di sacrificio. A me stasera De Bruyne non è del tutto soddisfatto perché quello che ci doveva dare, la qualità, non ce l’ha data. Si è sacrificato tanto, ma non ci serve questo da De Bruyne. Milinkovic sul primo gol va giù e deve rimanere in piedi, quella palla se rimane in piedi la prende, ma sul secondo si schiaccia proprio sul palo. Lui sbaglia la traslazione, si schiaccia sul palo, non può stare lì, deve lasciare un po’ di palo e coprire la porta. Il tiratore deve trovare lo specchio coperto, lui sbaglia la bisettrice, totalmente la traslazione, va sul palo e non è la prima volta che noto questo suo atteggiamento. Quel gol ce l’ha sulla coscienza. Ed è un peccato perché avevo appena finito di elogiarlo per la partita precedente. Ha mostrato personalità in uscita, qualche parata brutta ma efficace, ce n’è stata una nel primo tempo che mi ha fatto tremare, che l’ha presa in maniera raffazzonata, però aveva retto. Ma alla fine io penso che sia successo esattamente come 15 anni fa. L’ottimo De Sanctis, che a Napoli fece molto bene, in quella partita purtroppo non fu impeccabile e il Napoli, che meritava di vincerla con Mazzarri, la pareggiò 2-2. La stessa cosa capita 15 anni dopo, ancora il portiere non impeccabile. Gilmour è stato sicuramente tra i migliori in campo. Io premio Politano per il sacrificio e per la palla che dà a Spinazzola sulla destra, che è favolosa, ma Gilmour sicuramente ha fatto una grande partita, la migliore. Vorrei citare un giocatore nel suo ruolo, finalmente, centrale a due di difesa: Beukema ha dimostrato che non è un bidone e se Beukema prende fiducia, almeno con questo investimento possiamo pensare che torni qualcosa. Così come Lang forse è l’esterno che stavamo cercando e che, dandogli fiducia, ce l’abbiamo in casa”.

Io andavo allo stadio con il club Re Cecconi di Ostia, partendo da piazza Quarto dei Mille con il pullman organizzato e il panino con la frittata. Se poi Lotito deciderà effettivamente di realizzarlo oppure no, non posso saperlo: bisogna prima arrivare a quel momento. Ma, una volta ottenute tutte le autorizzazioni, possiamo riconoscere che avere lo stadio Flaminio nel cuore della città rappresenterebbe una grande opportunità di crescita per la Lazio? Credo proprio di sì. Oggi incontro tifosi che mi abbracciano e mi chiedono di non far realizzare lo stadio, mentre fino a due anni fa mi chiedevano esattamente il contrario. By WILL PICKWORTH, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 06:20 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 06:30 EST, 21 November 2026.

The goalkeeper involved in the collision that killed Spanish footballer Jesus de Miguel has been seen in public for the first time since the tragic accident.

During a match earlier this month, Andorra keeper Jesus Owono came flying out of his goal and wiped out Tenerife star de Miguel with a high challenge which resulted in the striker being admitted to intensive care, where he later died.

De Miguel's passing shocked the footballing world and Owono was subsequently given a 12-match ban by authorities.

Both sides have been back in action since the tragedy, but on Friday, Andorra hosted Leganes at their Estadi de la FAF.

That was their first home game since de Miguel's passing, and they made sure to pay a moving tribute to him on the night.

Before the match, the players went onto the pitch wearing shirts with his name and number on them and they carried out a bouquet of white flowers.

Andorra keeper Jesus Owono was seen in public for the first time since Jesus de Miguel's tragic death as he attended a tribute to the former Tenerife star.

Before Andorra's game with Legannes, several tributes were paid, including a minute's silence.

A minute's silence was also held before the game, while those in attendance applauded during the ninth minute of the match, the shirt number worn by de Miguel at Tenerife.

The most striking part of the evening though was Owono's attendance in the stands.

The goalkeeper has stayed away from the public eye since de Miguel's death, after which he was subjected to chants of 'murderer', but he wanted to attend the tribute at his club's home ground.

Owono was wearing a black coat and hat as he stood next to team-mates who weren't involved in the matchday squad.

Despite receiving the support of the crowd and his team-mates, local reports noted Owono cut a downcast figure and that he was seen praying immediately after the minute's silence.

Owono's desire to attend the tribute came after he had also asked to meet de Miguel's family, something he hopes to do one day.

Meanwhile, Tenerife returned to action last week against AD Ceuta CF in a match that was also filled with tributes.

Players provided a floral tribute as they arrived for the match, and gathered outside gate nine of the Heliodoro Rodríguez Lopez Stadium – another nod to de Miguel's shirt number.

Grief-stricken Tenerife stars then took to the field carrying a bouquet of flowers, and placed it at the scene of the tragedy.

Both sets of players and fans then observed a minute's silence in memory of de Miguel before the game kicked off.

The game was then brought to a pause in the ninth minute, so the players could pay another tribute.

Fans inside the stadium unveiled a tifo which read: 'Jesus de Miguel, 9, eternal blanquiazul', which translates to: 'Jesus de Miguel, 9, eternally white and blue.'.

Other fans held up white and blue cards beside the tifo, with others in the ground applauding. When Tenerife scored, de Miguel's shirt was held in the air.

After the game, which Tenerife won 2-0, both teams gathered in the centre circle to place de Miguel's shirt on a bouquet of flowers, and the fans applauded to bring an end to an emotional day.

Owono was watching the game from the stands as he stood next to some of his team-mates.

Tenerife returned to action last week and paid several tributes to their former star de Miguel.

The tragedy occurred as the game between Tenerife and Andorra entered the seventh minute of stoppage time, when de Miguel looked set to race away on the counter-attack for his side in search of a winner.

As he watched a long ball drop into his path, the striker was struck in the chest by Owono's flying knee as he attempted to clear the ball near the halfway line.

After initially rolling around on the floor, de Miguel became motionless, and medical staff rushed onto the pitch to attend to him.

Owono was given a red card for the challenge before the decision was soon taken by the referee to abandon the fixture.

Owono's 12-match ban is presently in effect, yet his manager Carles Manso hinted that he may never play again.

He said: 'We will ​give him space so that he feels completely free to make ‌any ⁠decision, whether he wants to return, when, or if he does not want to return.

'When he feels it is appropriate and when ​he feels genuinely ready to take a ​decision ⁠like that (he will do so).'.

Tottenham Hotspur have never before in the club’s history begun a league season without scoring a single goal in the first four games, although having done so after spending £329m on latest players really does take some doing.

“Please score a goal!” was the homemade sign from two Spurs fans upon which the television cameras lingered at the end of the game, although the jaunty felt-tip design and glued-on team crest were rather upbeat compared to the gloom of the stadium. Spurs have tried to outrun their past but it just keeps catching up with them.

A team reimagined, a manager freshly released and yet they are back in the same grip of anxiety that accompanied them on two consecutive 17th-place finishes in the last two seasons. By the end of this they might have been glad to escape with a single point against Everton, the one team in the Premier League who closed the window with a net transfer profit.

In a recent development, for Roberto De Zerbi, there was another passionate defence of his team afterwards. “The people, the fans already understand if I make excuses or not,” he noted. “I came last season when the s--- was like this”, he gestured to a level somewhere around the midpoint of his forehead. “I have always been… not positive but realistic. I am sorry for the result that it’s not immediately the improvement. We played as a team. We didn’t score. We didn’t win [but] we played as a team.”.

Indeed he co-opted the Italian term “sbloccare” to describe his team’s problem. They simply need to unlock – or unblock – the team and the goals would flow. He joked that in Italy he would be lauded for two consecutive clean sheets in this game and the previous one against Nottingham Forest. “What did you write?” he demanded of one of the Italian newspaper correspondents. “You have the passport.”.

Spurs have one last game at home this month, on Saturday against Aston Villa, to end the streak in September. They were into the second half before the first attempt on target that obliged Jordan Pickford to make a save – Mateus Fernandes’s shot slapping limply against the Everton goalkeeper’s gloves to ironic cheers from the home fans.

At the end De Zerbi could not contain his frustration, unable to wait until he reached the privacy of the dressing room to tell Mathys Tel where he had gone wrong. He did so with the Spurs substitute still wiping the sweat from his brow on the pitch. The player did not look at all impressed. De Zerbi said later that he was simply reminding his player of what it took to play as a central striker.

“There is a term in Italian, ‘sbloccare’ that literally translates as ‘unblock’… I know we can score goals and win games. We have to respect the history of the players – if you forget [Dominic] Solanke and [Omar] Marmoush the others haven’t scored many in their careers. I think we can find the goals with the quality of the players.”.

Industry observers note that spurs play Liverpool at Anfield in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday before Villa a week today. The Spurs record at home is dismal. In the last 35 games they have won just five, drawn 10 and lost a remarkable 20. This new stadium has become a problem for the team in it – or maybe it is the other way around.

Hard to pick out any major chances – it was that kind of game – but Brennan Johnson should have won it for the away team in the second half. The ball was cut back to him by Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall and the former Spurs man skied his shot.

Like many of his team-mates, he had hung in there. There was another fine performance from Jarrad Branthwaite at centre-half and Moyes mentioned that he hoped it might earn him a place in the England squad. “He is still finding his way back from injury,” Moyes said, “it would be great if he could get a call-up.”.

In the directors’ box were the usual pained expressions of Vinai Venkatesham, the Spurs chief executive, and chairman Peter Charrington. They sat alongside Vivienne Lewis, daughter of the patriarch Joe. There is a certain fatigue about the home crowd when faced with afternoons like this which suggests they have seen so much that the bar is quite high – or low – to provoke a really splenetic response. Perhaps it is just too early in the season although the final whistle was met with boos.

In a recent development, the first shot on target of the entire game for either side was a free-kick struck by James Garner in added time at the end of the first half. Spurs had started at a ferocious pace although they could not sustain it.

De Zerbi complained about the pre-season injuries on tour in Australia and also the lack of time he had to integrate Sávio and Marmoush. He said that his team were not in the right “physical condition”.

“We played very well in the first 30 minutes and maybe the energy and the fact we didn’t score – we lost confidence.” By the end, he had sent on James Maddison, Tel, Lucas Bergvall and Mohammed Kudus to little avail. Everton looked more likely to win it.

According to recent reports, speaking to Sky Sports, the Everton defender said: “You look at the game from the start, they put us under pressure and we had to dig deep to stay in the game. In a recent development, mikel Arteta has laid bare his quirky management techniques so his players are ready for any eventuality. Late meals and making the dressing room hotter are among his tricks, although nothing can prepare a player having 40,000 fans calling you a “sad Geordie b------”.

What an key week it has been for Arsenal, who have shown their squad depth by winning in Napoli then travelling to the Stadium of Light and extending their perfect start to the season to six games.

It has been revealed that other teams with aspirations of the title dropped points earlier in the day, while Arteta could battle to a win with key players brought back into the team and Guimarães coming off the bench at half-time. A trip in the Champions League followed by an away game the following weekend is a barometer of where teams are, and Arsenal have sounded a warning after coming through a bruising encounter.

According to recent reports, régis Le Bris’s team offer a challenge that is impossible to replicate, even by the standards of Arteta’s “sabotage” to make his players uncomfortable. There were complaints of elbows being aimed at Gabriel Magalhães.

Bukayo Saka scored a stoppage-time penalty to seal the win but the evening belonged to Guimarães, the £75m summer signing who has been waiting for this moment to ignite his Arsenal career.

“Everyone knows I had a difficult start through injuries in my short time. But I’m glad to be back and glad to play,” Guimarães stated. “I feel very good. It was unbelievable to score a beautiful goal, beautiful moment for me and my family and I am happy.”.

According to recent reports, these are ominous signs for Arsenal’s title rivals, with Guimarães’s return to fitness adding to the midfield options. Recent findings suggest that and his players stood up to a physical challenge. Brian Brobbey used his frame to back into the Arsenal’s centre-backs, who are unlikely to given such a tough assignment this season aside from facing Erling Haaland.

Guimarães was brought on at half-time along with Jurriën Timber, which was another sign of Arsenal mounting a strong defence of their title. With Arteta’s changes altering the pace of the game, the match turned just before the hour mark. John Brooks saw nothing in the incident that floored Gabriel at a corner, but at the next set-piece penalised Ezri Konsa for wrestling with Dan Ballard, much to Arteta’s fury.

It has been revealed that le Fée had earned a point against Brentford a week earlier with a penalty, but this time his finish was tipped on to the post by David Raya. “We should not talk about the save of the keeper, we should talk about what happened before that,” added Arteta.

“But I loved the save from David, the way the team reacted, the way we go again and we go against everything, but this should never happen, it’s not fair, and I am sad, very sad, in that sense.”.

Sources indicate that raya also denied Nordi Mukiele from close range when Granit Xhaka’s expertly taken free-kick found his team-mate in front of goal. Sunderland have their own European campaign starting on Thursday and will start with confidence after pushing the champions all the way.

Brooks awarded a penalty in stoppage-time when Saka was brought down by Reinildo Mandava, who was dismissed. “I’m extremely pleased to win again. We had a really tough week, Chelsea, Napoli, winning there and now against a really tough opponent in a difficult place,” added Arteta.

Mikel Arteta released a furious attack on referee John Brooks for awarding a penalty against Arsenal and fears similar decisions will cost his team the Premier League title.

Brooks gave a spot-kick for Ezri Konsa tussling with Dan Ballard, although Arteta accused the Sunderland centre-back of a “judo roll”.

Enzo Le Fée’s penalty was saved by David Raya, with Arsenal winning after goals from Bruno Guimarães and Bukayo Saka.

According to recent reports, “In my opinion, that is not acceptable. I watched it 20 times,” noted Arteta. “And I cannot find a way to understand how you think to give a penalty in that situation or the way the VAR has to intervene.

Industry observers note that “I’m sad that we have to discuss something in such a beautiful game at this level. That has gravity because that changes the course of the season and it can cost you the championship. And at this level, with all the work that we put in, this cannot happen.

It has been revealed that “You see, it is a judo roll and it brings the player on the floor. So how can this happen? I cannot find an explanation. That’s why I’m trying to find that.”.

The win rounded off a positive week for Arsenal despite Arteta’s fury at the officials.

“I’m extremely pleased to win again. We had a really tough week, Chelsea, Napoli, winning there and now against a really tough opponent in a difficult place. I’m very worried and very sad because this can never be a penalty ever.

When will Martin Zubimendi start again for Arsenal? Mikel Arteta wants to avoid a repeat of last season, when Zubimendi played more games than anyone in Europe, but it is curious that the Spaniard has not yet started a single match of this campaign. It is one thing to reduce his minutes, and another to turn him into a permanent substitute.

In a recent development, zubimendi has looked quite good off the bench in recent games but has been behind Myles Lewis-Skelly and Mikel Merino in the battle to partner Declan Rice from the start. And that’s before Bruno Guimaraes, the fresh £75m signing, reaches full fitness.

Industry observers note that in the thick Naples air in midweek, Declan Rice did what he always does: he kept running. Another start for the Arsenal midfielder, another 90 minutes completed and another performance of constructive passing and destructive defending. For anyone who was worried about Rice’s physical condition, it was an emphatic response.

After that Champions League victory over Napoli, Rice insisted he was ready for another marathon campaign. He made 69 appearances for club and country last season, up from 60 the previous term, and believes that is a sustainable number of games, even for an all-action midfielder such as himself. “I have shown I can do it,” he noted.

The key question, though, is not whether Rice can do it, but whether he should do it. There is no doubt that his body eventually began to pay the price for his exertions last year, especially during the World Cup, and it would be reasonable for his managers to worry that his extraordinary workload might one day take a serious toll. This, after all, is a footballer who managed nerve pain in his hamstring throughout the second half of last season.

Regis Le Bris, who made 11 changes for the League Cup win over Hull in midweek, reverts to the starting XI that drew at Brentford seven days ago.

Hello and welcome to live, minute-by-minute coverage of Sunderland v Arsenal at the Stadium of Light. Sunderland are the latest team tasked with stopping Arsenal, who have begun their title defence in formidable style: they’ve won out of three, including a dominant comeback victory against Chelsea last weekend, and look well equipped to become the first Arsenal team to retain the title since the mid-1930s.

Industry observers note that there’s a long way to go, and Arsenal fans will remember how blisteringly they started their last two title defences in 2002-03 and 2004-05, only to ultimately fall short. But right now, they could barely be in better shape. Their fine start to the season came with a Champions League win in Naples, achieved despite a delay to their flight from London.

Recent findings suggest that “I love those challenges,” said Mikel Arteta. “I try to create them in pre-seasons so when they happen, we already experience them and we already know. So get to the stadium very late, change the routine and suddenly the players have to do something else.

“Because when it happens, and it can happen, you can miss the flight, the train can be delayed, there’s so much traffic and I don’t want the players, but not only the players, the staff as well, panicking. So when that happens, adapt to it.”.

Arteta has tested his squad in a variety of ways. “[We have] delayed the meals, delayed the transport, taken a different route. We’ve done many things – made the dressing room hotter, more difficult, more challenging, less beds... because we’re going to have to adapt to different contexts.”.

So far, they’re adapting very well to the context of being the reigning champions.

Alla vigilia della sfida casalinga di Champions League contro lo Stoccarda, Cristian Chivu è intervenuto come di consueto in conferenza stampa, tornando anche sul pareggio per 4-4 contro l'Atalanta dell'ultimo turno di campionato: "L'Inter non può essere giudicata per uno spezzone di una partita", ha dichiarato, invitando il gruppo a un'analisi lucida per correggere gli errori. Il tecnico della Beneamata ha al contempo difeso la competitività della rosa, escludendo la necessità di cercare alibi nel calendario o nel mercato: "Abbiamo doppi ruoli in qualsiasi posizione, abbiamo un centrocampista in più addirittura".

It has been revealed that sulla stessa linea Nicolò Barella, che ha riconosciuto alcune difficoltà nella gestione dei momenti della partita e nella capacità di mantenere alta l'attenzione per tutti i novanta minuti. "Il fatto che l'Inter sia considerata forte e debba stare a livelli alti lo accettiamo e ne siamo felici. Vuol dire che la valutazione è alta e ce la teniamo. Non accetto però il disfattismo che c'è ogni volta verso di noi quando succede qualcosa che non ci si aspetta. Bisogna avere un equilibrio, e bisogna pensare che chi va in campo non è sempre al 100%. Questo è il calcio, non penso che ogni volta all'Inter succeda qualcosa di strano". L'obiettivo è ritrovare continuità e concentrazione, affrontando con la giusta mentalità tutti gli impegni stagionali.

Intanto arrivano aggiornamenti sulle condizioni di Hakan Calhanoglu, costretto a fermarsi durante la gara contro l'Atalanta. Gli esami strumentali effettuati all'Istituto Clinico Humanitas di Rozzano hanno evidenziato un risentimento muscolare ai flessori della coscia destra. L'Inter non ha ancora comunicato i tempi di recupero del centrocampista turco, che intanto salterà dunque la sfida con lo Stoccarda.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Vincenzo Montella, ex allenatore del Milan, ha rilasciato una intervista a La Gazzetta dello Sport, ricordando i suoi tempi in rossonero.

Com'era il rapporto con Berlusconi?

According to recent reports, "A Berlusconi piaceva parlare di calcio, gli piaceva dare suggerimenti anche quando l'allenatore era un po' fuori contesto in quel momento, perché lui aveva sempre la mentalità di avere Van Basten centravanti — Pallone d'Oro — e in panchina il sostituto, Papin. Questo me lo ricordo benissimo: lui voleva che giocassimo con due punte e io cercavo di tamponare per mesi (gli attaccanti erano, Kalinie e André Silva). È difficile perché io facevo le formazioni, è difficile sbagliare formazione perché io me le ricordo tutte. Ero tifoso del Milan, quindi il titolare era Van Basten e la riserva era Papin, entrambi Palloni d'Oro. Quindi, gli dicevo, 'Se lei mi compra qualche giocatore così, stia tranquillo che li faccio giocare tutti e due'".

10 anni fa arrivava la Supercoppa a Doha.

"È stato un anno in cui siamo tornati in Europa, credo fossero due o tre anni che il Milan non ci andava, ed era qualcosa di nuovo all'epoca. Abbiamo vinto un trofeo, piccolo: proprio qualche sera fa ho vistoa cena Galliani e me l'ha ricordato e lo ricordo perfettamente. Ecco, se devo dire, ho trovato un dirigente all'epoca perfetto, perché quando accompagnava qualche aneddoto su queste pressioni, stava sempre dalla mia parte, mi lasciava autonomia totale nelle scelte. Mi ha aiutato dal numero dei collaboratori a nuove cose: qualsiasi cosa chiedessi, era sempre dalla parte dell'allenatore. E quindi per me è stato un dirigente incredibile, che in quella fase lì, in quel cambio lì, è stato fondamentale anche per ottenere quei piccoli risultati, soprattutto dopo il grande Milan di Berlusconi. Noi meritavamo di vincere anche durante i tempi regolamentari: avevamo avuto alcune opportunità facili per chiuderla, poi siamo arrivati ai rigori. Gigio parò il rigore a Dybala, che calciò bello forte, ma lui la porta gliel'ha riempita".

Poi c'è stato il mercato delle cose formali...

"Io dall'inizio era un po' preoccupato perché c'è questa mania di esternare tutto, di — insomma — quasi pubblicitario più che altro, quindi era un po' preoccupato. In teoria c'era condivisione, almeno così si palesava, ma non potevo tirarmi indietro quando in realtà non era sempre così. E quindi alcune volte c'erano dei calciatori per cui non ero neanche stato consultato, che arrivavano e che poi dicevano 'È stato condiviso': quando sei lì non puoi dire diversamente. Sicuramente, quando si costruisce una squadra e hai il budget, la prima cosa che fai è: il portiere ce l'avevamo, prendo un centravanti, ci manca il centravanti. Nella scelta di tutto era rimasto il centravanti, con un budget — se non ricordo male — sui quindici-venti milioni. E quindi poi Kalinić... lui sì, l'ho scelto io perché quello era il budget. Quindi la nostra, diciamo, seconda scelta di attaccante fu pagato trentotto milioni, se non ricordo male, che era André Silva, e il primo attaccante fu la metà. E quindi, se non ricordo male, si è creato un equivoco di questo tipo, con tanti cambi, che poi in quella fase non giocavamo neanche male per avere, credo, quindici giocatori nuovi. Avevamo ancora Calhanoglu che non stava bene, che veniva da sei mesi di inattività per squalifica, se non ricordo male: quindi, nel contesto, era in costruzione la squadra; non eravamo in linea con gli obiettivi dello scudetto che erano stati proclamati, ma sicuramente per un processo di crescita eravamo assolutamente in linea".

"All'epoca forse stavamo trattando Aubameyang, se non ricordo male".

Cristiano Ronaldo, si parlava anche di lui: ci credevi?

“No, non credevo: anzi, proprio per nulla".

Avevi contatti con la proprietà cinese?

"Siamo andati lì, erano proprietari. Col senno di poi magari diverso, però allora non erano, come dire, nocivi".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tutte le novità per la Supercoppa Italiana dal 2027 al 2030: si riparte dalla gara secca, ma resta l'opzione estero.

Sources indicate that la Lega Calcio Serie A ha ufficialmente approvato e reso pubblico il bando per i diritti audiovisivi della Supercoppa Italiana sul territorio italiano per il triennio 2027/28, 2028/29 e 2029/30, disegnando un quadro che lega strettamente aspetti sportivi e ritorni economici. Il primo cambiamento strutturale è la separazione della Supercoppa dalla Coppa Italia nella vendita dei diritti, una scelta che dà alla competizione un percorso commerciale autonomo per i prossimi tre anni.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Recent findings suggest that per chi si aggiudicherà i diritti televisivi, la novità principale è la possibilità esclusiva di acquistare anche il pacchetto di title sponsorship legato al torneo. Non è fissato un prezzo minimo di partenza: le emittenti dovranno formulare una propria offerta economica, indicando anche un corrispettivo aggiuntivo in caso di formula a quattro squadre. Chi otterrà questo abbinamento potrà legare il proprio nome alla competizione e al premio per il migliore in campo, oltre a ottenere visibilità a bordocampo, sul trofeo e sulla patch applicata alla manica destra delle maglie delle squadre partecipanti. Sul fronte della trasmissione, le eventuali semifinali potranno andare in onda anche a pagamento, mentre per la finale restano fermi gli obblighi di diffusione in chiaro previsti dalla normativa sugli eventi di particolare rilevanza sociale.

Sul piano del calendario, la Lega cercherà un'intesa con il licenziatario per stabilire il periodo di svolgimento del torneo, ma si riserva comunque l'ultima parola se non si dovesse raggiungere un accordo. Come criterio base il bando riporta la Supercoppa alla formula tradizionale della gara secca tra la vincitrice del campionato e quella della Coppa Italia, fissando un prezzo minimo di 8 milioni di euro a stagione (24 milioni complessivi nel triennio). Resta però aperta la strada della Final Four: la Lega può scegliere a propria discrezione di attivarla in una o più stagioni del bando, con le prime due classificate in campionato e le due finaliste di Coppa Italia (e l'eventuale ripescaggio di terza e quarta in Serie A), incassando in quel caso 7 milioni di euro in più per ciascuna edizione. A pesare sulla decisione tra finale a due o a quattro sarà soprattutto la sede, dato che resta la possibilità di giocare sia in Italia sia all'estero.

Inside Diego Gomez's remarkable rise to Premier League's king of the wondergoal: Plucked from a rural Paraguayan village at 13, doing Lionel Messi's running for him at Inter Miami and starring as Brighton's aggressive machine

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1460 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 02:00 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 08:07 EST, 21 November 2026.
  • Scattered across the flatlands of Paraguay’s deeply religious Misiones District, where families rely on the land to feed themselves through cattle ranching and cotton production, the people are idolising one of their own.
  • Sources indicate that diego Gomez’s ascent from the humble beginnings of a farmer’s son to the heart of a Premier League title race is a Hollywood director’s dream.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By TARA ANSON-WALSH, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 02:00 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 08:07 EST, 21 November 2026.

Scattered across the flatlands of Paraguay’s deeply religious Misiones District, where families rely on the land to feed themselves through cattle ranching and cotton production, the people are idolising one of their own.

Sources indicate that diego Gomez’s ascent from the humble beginnings of a farmer’s son to the heart of a Premier League title race is a Hollywood director’s dream. While it is a script that has been read many times before, like an old movie or a classic song, it is also one that never gets old.

Industry observers note that in this particular iteration, it begins on the dirt tracks of Mburika Reta, which literally translates to the ‘land of donkeys’ in Paraguay’s native Guarani, before winding through the country's capital, Asuncion, and briefly stopping among the palm-lined suburbs of Miami alongside Sergio Busquets and Lionel Messi. It is now gathering pace on England’s south coast, where Brighton find themselves in the unfamiliar territory of hunting down the Premier League champions.

Industry observers note that gomez is the epitome of Fabian Hurzeler’s machine: energetic, aggressive and relentlessly forward-thinking. It is through this collective sense of selflessness that the Seagulls are second in the table, having already defeated both league leaders Arsenal and Manchester City this season. And for Hurzeler’s versatile midfielder, every performance and goal is a reminder of the moments that forged him.

‘He always told me to play forward and, when I have the ball, to have no fear,’ the 23-year-old stated last year of his former team-mate Messi.

Cue a spectacular goal from the halfway line against Crystal Palace last month, the Amex crowd growing feverish as the ball sailed over Walter Benitez before crashing into the back of the net.

Diego Gomez pictured as a young teen playing for Libertad (left), is now thriving for Paraguay (right) and one of Brighton's most important players.

Gomez is congratulated by Pascal Gross after scoring a brilliant goal against Brentford.

Another quickly followed against Brentford last weekend, with Gomez barely bringing the ball under control before hooking it into the net from 25 yards out with his supposedly weaker left foot, leaving half of his team-mates clutching their heads in disbelief.

Inevitably Gomez’s rise has not been without its setbacks. It was his mistimed tackle on Desire Doue, stretching out a leg to topple the French winger in the penalty area, that led to the heartache of Paraguay’s World Cup elimination this summer, after Kylian Mbappe slotted home the resulting spot-kick.

Yet rather than be defined by this mistake, Gomez returned home to a hero’s welcome, mobbed by locals as he was paraded through the streets of the usually sleepy San Juan Bautista in an open-top car.

In a recent development, ‘He has the right attitude towards football,’ Hurzeler stated shortly after his arrival. ‘He loves to play. You can feel his passion in every talk with him.’.

Across his 10 appearances this season, Gomez has won 66 duels, more than any Brighton player. His 35 aerial duels won, second behind only Croatian centre back Luka Vuskovic, point to his impressive spring, and he has won 10 tackles, again more than any other Brighton player.

At the other end of the pitch, meanwhile, he has taken the most touches in the opposition box and has scored two goals and recorded two assists this season.

While Gomez’s physique gives the impression of a battering ram, he is surprisingly speedy, recording Brighton’s fastest top speed of the season against Chelsea at 21.01mph.

Sources indicate that but who is this kid who was plucked out of nowhere? Who, at the age of 13, moved four hours away from his rural village to the capital to play football, navigating the bus networks as a child to get to training at FC Libertad before a move to join David Beckham’s glitzy side arrived seven years later?

Gomez, seen with his partner Geraldine Villagra, has taken an unusual route to the top.

Industry observers note that in this case, it was Inter Miami who did the plucking, with Gomez identified by Brighton’s scouting network while he was playing in the MLS in 2024. Gomez formally joined the club as a 21-year-old in a deal worth £11million in January 2025, having agreed the move six months earlier.

Recent findings suggest that former Brighton centre back Gordon Greer is now the club’s pathway development manager and spoke regularly to Gomez during this time, travelling to Florida to see him during the latter stages of the MLS season. It’s fair to say he liked what he found.

‘We knew that he would do well because of his application,’ Greer claims. ‘He was just a really talented, young, hungry footballer. You could see that he had raw potential, and I think Brighton do that really well. They sign players who have got room to improve.

Recent findings suggest that ‘The one thing about Diego that is really impressive is his attitude, his work rate. He’s a really driven character and he’s such a humble kid. You can ask Diego to do certain things and he’ll give it his all, no matter what you ask him to do, whether he’s good at it or not. As a coach, it must be amazing to have someone like that in your team.’.

During his six-month wait for the move, Gomez undertook regular English lessons, tuned in to Brighton’s games on television and spoke to Hurzeler about the areas he could improve before making the switch. All of that left him with a couple of weeks’ head start, which in Premier League terms is massive.

Meanwhile, Brighton’s plethora of South American footballers at the time, most notably Julio Enciso, who played alongside him at Libertad, helped him settle quickly. So too did Gomez’s girlfriend, Geraldine Villagra, who moved to Brighton to live with him, while his family regularly visit from Paraguay.

Gomez is the epitome of Fabian Hurzeler’s energetic machine for the Seagulls.

According to recent reports, spending 18 months alongside Messi, Busquets and Luis Suarez was also another key step in Gomez’s development, despite his understandable initial nerves. He forged a strong understanding with Messi on the pitch and was the engine that enabled the Argentine genius to thrive. Much like at Brighton, though, that did not stop Gomez from producing moments of magic of his own.

In a recent development, ‘The fact that he had these superstars in the team probably helped him,’ Greer says. ‘We don’t have any superstars in our team like Messi, but everyone gives their all.

Recent findings suggest that ‘At Inter Miami, Messi was by far the best player, but Diego did a lot of the running for him and had a fantastic season in which he contributed a number of goals and assists. He just worked away at it. Regardless of the kind of environment you put him in, he finds a way through it.’.

The audacity of Gomez’s two recent goals, the strike against Palace that inevitably won the Premier League Goal of the Month award for October and the Brentford one which is firmly in contention for November, almost contradicts that industrious nature. Has Greer been surprised by them?

According to recent reports, ‘He scored some really good goals for Inter Miami, but not as good as the ones he’s scored of late for us,’ he states. ‘He wants to achieve massive things. It’s no surprise... well, it is a surprise when you see him stick one in the top corner with his left foot!’.

Gomez endeared himself to many when he broke down during a pre-World Cup press conference while speaking about the privilege of representing his country, and he remains deeply aware of where he has come from.

Earlier this year, Brighton chose to extend their UNICEF partnership to Paraguay, with Gomez becoming an ambassador for a programme that aims to develop young people's skills and confidence through sport and will reach thousands of children across the nation, a role he regards as a great honour.

After Paraguay’s elimination from the World Cup, Gomez attended one of the events in Asuncion, where he first plied his trade and where UNICEF will soon roll out the programme.

‘During his personal time, after coming back from the World Cup, he could have done lots of other things and chose instead to do that,’ Anna Easthope, Brighton’s head of marketing, adds. ‘He realises the impact of meeting kids, giving them inspiration and letting them know that sport is for everyone.’.

If a hero’s welcome followed World Cup elimination, imagine the reception a Premier League title would bring to Misiones.

  • I Am Naples Testata Giornalistica - aut.

It has been revealed that enzo Maresca, allenatore del Manchester City, ha rilasciato alcune dichiarazioni in conferenza stampa dopo il pareggio in Champions League contro il Napoli.:  “Noi cerchiamo sempre di vincere, ma se non puoi vincere è importante non perdere. Prendiamo il punto, ne abbiamo 10 in classifica e in fin dei conti è un buon risultato per andare avanti. Ricordo un loro calcio d’angolo e i due gol, in questo momento gli avversari sono cinici davanti alla porta. C’è poco da fare, accettiamo il punto e andiamo avanti. L’impatto sui giocatori? In questo momento va un po’ così, le prime dieci partite siamo stati sempre noi a sbloccare, mentre ora sono gli avversari a farlo. Non credo che abbia un impatto sulla fiducia dei calciatori, devi correre un po’ di più se sei in svantaggio, ma abbiamo lottato fino alla fine e serve alzare l’asticella. Non dobbiamo subire questi gol, basta vedere le statistiche a nostro favore. C’è uno squilibrio tra le occasioni create e i gol segnati. Anche Cherki ha detto che mancava energia? Siamo stati molto aggressivi. I due terzini in posizione centrale? Abbiamo iniziato con Bouaddi e Enzo in mezzo per vedere se potevamo trovare equilibrio, poi Nico e Matheus Nunes hanno fatto bene, è un’altra opzione per noi. Volevamo fare qualche cambio ed essere più fisici in mezzo al campo per contrastarli. La qualità del gol di Cherki? Ottimo, sono contento per lui. Ha fatto bene, sappiamo che sa giocare meglio centralmente, ma sta facendo bene. Ci aspettavamo un Napoli col blocco basso, era difficile trovare soluzioni, ma dovevamo evitare di concedere i gol concessi, erano evitabili. I cori a Donnarumma? Non ci ho fatto caso, ero concentrato sulla partita. Era difficile attaccare il Napoli, erano in undici sulla linea dell’area. Potevamo fare meglio nelle chance avute e cercare di evitare le due occasioni concesse. Hanno avuto quelle e il corner di Beukema, c’è rammarico per non aver vinto, ma se non puoi farlo è importante anche non perdere. Non vinciamo da tre partite, ma i meriti del Napoli sono importanti: si è difeso bene e ha concretizzato due occasioni. Noi potevamo fare meglio, il Napoli ha avuto i suoi meriti e ha fatto una buona gara”.

Woeful Man Utd have no excuses, Carrick is under substantial pressure
