📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, QPR swooped to sign the stopper on loan from Manchester City in the summer. He has since become the Hoops’ number one and has made a positive impression with the London outfit in the Championship.

Charles, 21, has made 17 appearances for the Hoops in all competitions to date this season, 16 of which have come in the league, and he has kept four clean sheets. The R’s are presently in the play-offs along with Wolves, Birmingham City, West Brom, Southampton and Swansea City, with the likes of West Ham and Sheffield United chasing them down.

Maxwell has delivered his verdict on Charles on the Not The Top 20 Podcast on YouTube: “In terms of a goalkeeper’s passing range and ability, I’ve quite simply never seen anything like this with Charles. We’re talking about dropping passes wherever he wants, on a dime, on a sixpence, with both feet, on different trajectories.”.

He added: “We really need to enjoy him while we can, I don’t think he’ll be playing in the Championship after this season. Player like this are genuinely the reason why you fall in love with the game.”.

Sources indicate that QPR’s decision to bring in Charles in the last transfer window has worked out well for them. He has settled into life with the Hoops well and has become their first choice.

The Northern Ireland international, who has 18 caps to his name, was on the books at Sheffield Wednesday from 2021 to 2026. He went on to play 36 matches for the Owls, 21 of which came in the last campaign.

Charles was snapped up by Manchester City on a long-term deal in July. He was then given the green light to head out the exit door on a temporary basis to join the R’s.

City will be pleased with his development under Julien Stephan. He has enjoyed plenty of game time at QPR and is getting plenty of valuable experience under his belt.

Charles’ ability with the ball at his feet makes him the perfect modern day goalkeeper. At the age of just 21 still, he has potential to get even better down the line.

QPR should savour him while they can this term as they eye promotion to the top flight. Manchester City will have a big decision to make on what to do with him when he returns to the Etihad Stadium.

Recent findings suggest that if the Hoops go up, they will fancy their chances of re-signing him again. If they stay in the EFL though, it seems unlikely he would come back for a second spell.

Stephan’s side won 1-0 away at Millwall last time out with Nicolas Madsen getting their winner against the Lions at The Den in the first-half. They are back in action on Tuesday with an away trip to Norwich City.

After a humiliating defeat by Grimsby Town in their previous League Cup campaign, Manchester United found a different way to exit the competition this time around. The jeers heard at the full-time whistle after throwing away a two-goal lead pointed to more worrying times a year on from Blundell Park.

For the first time in half a century, United lost a game at Old Trafford having led 2-0, highlighting the defensive problems Michael Carrick needs to solve after turning results around last season.

“What the f---ing hell was that?” shouted the home fans, in a chant that may have been aimed at the referee but equally applied to United’s players, who led through Shea Lacey and Mason Mount’s early goals.

Brighton cut through Carrick’s defence several times before staging their comeback with goals from Charalampos Kostoulas, Pascal Gross and Maxim De Cuyper. Carrick and his analysts will rewatch the footage of all three goals in horror at how they conceded.

In a recent development, kostoulas halves the deficit! 🔵Brighton score on the stroke of half-time. pic.twitter.com/bGjN1w6s6c.

“I totally understand the feelings of the supporters,” Carrick said. “We have to accept it. I totally accept it. It’s on me ultimately: as a team what we look like, how we play and what results you get. I take that. I’ll take the praise, I’ll take the criticism and the upset.”.

Erik ten Hag used the domestic cups to taste success while struggling in the Premier League, but one of those opportunities is now lost to Carrick, who must be careful not to spiral from a poor start to the campaign into crisis. Sunday’s trip to Fulham before the international break now feels like a significant game for United and Carrick.

Recent findings suggest that “We’ve gone out of the cup and the feeling around the place feels bigger than that,” Carrick remarked. “I’ll be honest about that, that’s how it feels, but it doesn’t have to be like that. If we win football matches again, it can go in a different direction.

According to recent reports, “We have a significant game on Sunday that we have to prepare for. We’re out of this competition and we have to go back to winning football matches.

In a recent development, “It doesn’t feel good at the moment. It doesn’t feel good. We have to go back to winning football matches. We want to win and want to win swiftly. The next game is Sunday. That’s all I’m thinking about right now.”.

According to recent reports, at the start of the evening it seemed that the tie would be remembered for Lacey scoring on his first start for United, the first teenager to do so since Marcus Rashford. In the week when JJ Gabriel, one of United’s great academy talents, asked to leave the club, a different United teenager was kissing the badge when he found the net.

Sources indicate that gross took his chance when United carelessly played the ball out of defence again, with Diogo Dalot’s clearance mishit. Luka Vuskovic’s header went straight into the United penalty area, with their centre-backs failing to react promptly enough.

According to recent reports, “We take it how it is. According to recent reports, for Carrick, matches such as this can define a United manager’s reign if he cannot turn results around. The image of Ruben Amorim in the dugout at Grimsby was one of the lasting impressions of last season before Carrick was brought in to salvage the campaign.

Giving Youri Tielemans a £35m release clause looks like an error... Aston Villa toiling to a draw with Sunderland was more proof Unai Emery could do with a midfield controller in January, writes TOM COLLOMOSSE

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (910 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 12:22 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 14:14 EST, 21 November 2026.
  • Whoever put that £35million release clause in Youri Tielemans’ contract has a heck of a lot to think about these days.
  • The Belgian midfielder left Aston Villa to join Manchester United last summer and though these are early days in his Old Trafford career, the move does not seem to be working out for anyone.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By TOM COLLOMOSSE, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 12:22 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 14:14 EST, 21 November 2026.

Whoever put that £35million release clause in Youri Tielemans’ contract has a heck of a lot to think about these days.

The Belgian midfielder left Aston Villa to join Manchester United last summer and though these are early days in his Old Trafford career, the move does not seem to be working out for anyone.

Unai Emery was distraught to lose Tielemans and against Sunderland, you could see why. Emery signed two central midfielders, Leon Goretzka and Joao Gomes, and has given more minutes to Ross Barkley.

None of the three gives him what Tielemans did and Villa may decide to move for another central player in January. Anything for a bit of cleverness in that part of the pitch.

Sources indicate that tielemans has struggled at United and it will be interesting to see what Mauricio Pochettino makes of him. He is no elite athlete and United supporters and pundits have criticised him because of it but he gave Emery what he craves above all else – control. Neither Gomes nor Goretzka has Tielemans’ passing range and Barkley looks more effective higher up the pitch.

According to recent reports, with Sunderland sitting deep here, Villa desperately needed a player who could read the game and create angles like Tielemans. Without him, their passing was slow and predictable, against a Sunderland side without key men Dominic Ballard, Granit Xhaka and Brian Brobbey.

Sunderland's Nordi Mukiele stretches for the ball but nobody could find the breakthrough.

Regis Le Bris saw his side pick up another point to follow their win over Chelsea before the international break - Sunderland now sit 18th.

It has been revealed that their only chance in the first half here fell to Emi Buendia, who won the ball high then failed to chip the back-pedalling Robin Roefs. In the second half, Ian Maatsen and substitute Ibrahim Mbaye shot far too close to the Sunderland goalkeeper, who tipped over another effort from Barkley.

Industry observers note that villa have still not lost in the league since they were beaten here by Nottingham Forest in September but teams aiming for the Champions League should put away Sunderland at home. And after 150 Premier League games at the helm, nobody will know that better than Emery.

Buendia reached Aston Villa immortality last May when he scored in the Europa League final and now he has his own banner.

‘It’s Buendia, with a beauty, on the banks of the Bosphorus’ read the slogan in the Holte End.

They will never forget that 3-0 win over Freiburg here but it is alarming just how quickly the team has split apart since then. Six months have passed since Istanbul but only two of the starting XI from that night – Buendia and Torres – were in Unai Emery’s line-up here.

Emi Buendia is now the subject of a banner from Villa fans for his Europa League final heroics.

Youri Tielemans scored a stunner in the Europa League final but is now at Man United.

It has been revealed that true, Matty Cash and Victor Lindelof were injured, while John McGinn was left on the bench, with one eye on Tuesday’s return to Istanbul to face Galatasaray in the Champions League. Boubacar Kamara missed the final through injury.

Industry observers note that still these are huge changes. For most of Emery’s first four years at Villa, every player knew his role and understood the kind of team they were. Now Villa find themselves learning on the job in a three-sided ground, due to the improvement work that leaves the North Stand empty.

Emery knows it too. ‘We have brought a significant number of fresh players to the squad, many of whom are still adapting to the demands of competing at the level we have worked so hard to establish ourselves at.

ASTON VILLA (4-2-3-1): Suzuki 6; Wan-Bissaka 6, Harwood-Bellis 6, Torres 7, Maatsen 6; Kamara 6, Goretzka 5 (Barkley 73, 6); Alysson 6, Buendia 6 (McGinn 60, 7), Manzambi 5 (Mbaye 60, 6); Jackson 6 (Madjo 73, 6).

SUNDERLAND (4-2-3-1): Roefs 7; Meunier 7, Mukiele 7, O’Nien 7, Reinildo 7; Ahoka 8, Sadiki 7; Hume 6, Le Fee 7, Talbi 7; Isidor 7 (Angulo 77, 6).

'It takes time, patience, hard work and belief.

Sources indicate that ‘That is why, now more than ever, we must stick together, trust the direction we are heading in and continue to get behind our players and staff. Results are hugely notable but so is recognising the hard work and development that will help us keep moving forward.’.

These days clubs like Sunderland cannot afford to wait for young talents to prove themselves in other European leagues.

Recent findings suggest that A decade ago, clubs in the middle of the Premier League could sign players like that for relatively small sums. Now everyone in Europe knows how rich top flight clubs in England are and adjust their prices accordingly.

That is why Sunderland paid nearly £10million for Jules Ahoka even though he had barely played a senior game for Royal Antwerp.

According to recent reports, on this evidence, the Black Cats have spent wisely yet again. Ahoka is quick, athletic and strong – exactly what is required in English football today – and his technique is tidy too. If he stays healthy, a bright future awaits.

Latest Update: Swansea City identify manager with 2.32 points per game as leading contender to replace Vitor Matos

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (654 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that swansea City are pursuing a newly introduced head coach after Vitor Matos left his role at the Swansea.com Stadium to take charge of RC Strasbourg.
  • Sources indicate that according to a report from The Telegraph, the club have identified Icelandic manager Freyr Alexandersson as the leading candidate for their vacant head coach position.
  • Recent findings suggest that alexandersson is currently the manager of Norwegian side Rosenborg BK, who appointed him on a three-year contract in June.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that swansea City are pursuing a newly introduced head coach after Vitor Matos left his role at the Swansea.com Stadium to take charge of RC Strasbourg. Ashley Williams, Leon Britton, Joe Allen and Kris O’Leary are leading the Swans on an interim basis, but ground is swiftly being made in the search for a new boss.

Sources indicate that according to a report from The Telegraph, the club have identified Icelandic manager Freyr Alexandersson as the leading candidate for their vacant head coach position. Talks have been held between the 44-year-old and the Championship club, and he appears to be their prime target at present.

Recent findings suggest that alexandersson is currently the manager of Norwegian side Rosenborg BK, who appointed him on a three-year contract in June. He has overseen 14 wins in his 19 games in charge of the club, recording a points-per-game rate of 2.32.

In a recent development, alexandersson is a 44-year-old coach who has held a variety of roles in the dugout since beginning his coaching career back in 2008. He spent seven years at Leiknir Reykjavik as a player before moving into management.

In a recent development, the Swansea City target started out in women’s football, managing club team Valur before a short spell in charge of former club Leiknir Reykjavik. Alongside this role, Alexandersson spent five years as manager of the Iceland women’s national side.

Industry observers note that he then stepped into the men’s setup as an assistant to Erik Hamren and Arnar Vidarsson before a short spell as a No. 2 at Al-Arabi. From 2021 though, Alexandersson has worked strictly as a first-team boss in men’s football.

It has been revealed that he spent nearly three years in charge of Danish side Lyngby BK and 11 months at KV Kortrijk in Belgium before moving to SK Brann in Norway. Impressive work there saw him poached for the Rosenborg BK job, where he has continued to impress.

It has been revealed that swansea City head coach contender Alexandersson prioritises man management, working closely with his players to build strong relationships and placing importance on leadership. He has a strong reputation for developing players, which will appeal to the Swans too.

According to recent reports, tactically, his Rosenborg side set up in a 4-3-3 primarily, but he has used 5-3-2 or 3-5-2 formations in the past. Much like Matos, his teams press aggressively in the final third, and he demands frequent chance creation with players directed to suffocate opponents on and off the ball.

According to recent reports, in terms of tactical similarities, Alexandersson feels like a great fit for Swansea City. The fact he wants his players to press high and play forwards much like Matos means that there can be a smooth transition into the new management.

Bringing in a boss with completely different ideas could bring teething problems. This squad has been built to play on the front foot with and without the ball, and Alexandersson will ensure they do so.

Industry observers note that the Jamestown Analytics influence feels clear with this pursuit. They pride themselves on finding gems in lesser-used markets, and Alexandersson could be the latest top boss uncovered.

After initial talks, time will tell whether the Swans can strike a deal to bring Alexandersson to Wales.

AC Milan’s negotiating table has remained busy between the summer and winter windows, with a clear emphasis on contracts.

In the past month alone the club have announced new long-term deals for Strahinja Pavlovic and Christian Pulisic, and it believed that a couple more are not far from being announced. Extending the discussion to the youth teams, a lot of young talents have signed their first pro deals this year too.

Having been stung in the past by not preserving leverage when it comes to contracts, it marks a clear change in gear from the management to ensure that the prized assets for the present and future remain under control and do not slip away for nothing.

#187164. Man City are failing to give their supporters something to stand behind as Enzo Maresca's side radiate uncertainty with meek display in Fulham draw, writes JACK GAUGHAN

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (931 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dailymail ↗ Open Full Page

Man City are failing to give their supporters something to stand behind as Enzo Maresca's side radiate uncertainty with meek display in Fulham draw, writes JACK GAUGHAN

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (931 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 11:04 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 14:16 EST, 21 November 2026.
  • The bananas are disappearing now winter is coming, the fire and fury waning with each passing week.
  • Recent findings suggest that city were booed off at the end as Enzo Maresca ducked down the tunnel.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 11:04 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 14:16 EST, 21 November 2026.

The bananas are disappearing now winter is coming, the fire and fury waning with each passing week. In legal limbo, Manchester City’s supporters need something – anything – to stand behind but increasingly their team refuse to provide that solace.

Recent findings suggest that city were booed off at the end as Enzo Maresca ducked down the tunnel. Some of that could have been directed at referee Thomas Bramall, after Erling Haaland’s disallowed goal, but certainly a significant number were jeering what they’d just seen. That simply does not happen at the Etihad Stadium, even during the torrid run of two years ago.

But they are witnessing a squad who radiate uncertainty. Who take three touches when two will do; who always receive possession squarely facing their own goal; who do not create passing lines for their mates. And crucially, who are forever momentarily confused as to who exactly is picking up which runner and those split seconds make all the difference in this division.

In a recent development, there is just this strange state of unease around how they want to approach games at the moment, something that adversity can provoke and something that Maresca is adamant he can correct. A coach of his calibre should do given the time and freedom.

Yet when he spent the two-week international break studying clips and fashioning ways of improving, he cannot have envisaged a scenario whereby home fans were so incredulous at a lack of energy that they were roused to their feet when Haaland deigned to close down Bernd Leno and force an error.

Man City put in an underwhelming performance as they were held to a 1-1 draw by Fulham.

Enzo Maresca's side are radiating uncertainty and look worryingly vulnerable at the back.

Rodrigo Muniz made City pay as he put an impressive Fulham 1-0 ahead after 16 minutes.

Fulham popped it about nicely and at will. Found pockets to hurt their illustrious hosts, who were again asking a centre half – in this case Marc Guehi – to charge into midfield. City did have more balance than at Nottingham Forest for including Ayyoub Bouaddi for Enzo Fernandez, yet Alvaro Arbeloa still aggressively pressed them in that area to some success.

‘I told the players that we will have the chance to beat them if we play with courage,’ stated Arbeloa, who was indebted to the towering performance of defender David Affengruber.

Sources indicate that arsenal will have watched this grinning and could easily be racking up an unassailable lead once these teams meet in north London next Sunday. Unassailable with all the usual caveats about the appeal and what this season may or may not eventually mean.

City did create enough statistically but as with other games of late, that did not tell the whole story.

Calvin Bassey pirouetted through midfield, the heavily derided Gianluigi Donnarumma thwarting a number of strong Fulham chances, and City appeared somewhat lost and out of ideas.

Elliot Anderson equalised with a superb volley but City failed to create much after that.

Maresca expressed his concern at City's lack of clean sheets after they struggled again.

That is a worrying departure from recent defeats, where they attacked with the same abandon as that early season flourish when they might as well have hosted games at Madison Square Gardens and played with an orange ball.

MAN CITY (4-2-3-1): Donnarumma 7; Khusanov 6, Dias 6, Guehi 5, O’Reilly 5 (Gvardiol 78); Anderson 7, Bouaddi 7 (Fernandez 85); Ndiaye 6 (Allan 78), Foden 7 (Cherki 70), Doku 5; Haaland 5.

FULHAM (4-2-3-1): Leno 6; Tete 6, Affengruber 8, Bassey 7, Sessegnon 7 (Palacios 83); Berge 6, Charles 7; Bobb 7 (Garcia 78), King 6 (Larsson 70, 6), Iwobi 7 (Robinson 70, 6); Muniz 7 (Cairney 83).

Met with a Fulham who had not conceded more than once in the league since the start of September, City failed to create a meaningful opportunity in the last 25 minutes of a match they were desperate to win and should have been in the ascendancy of after Elliot Anderson’s volleyed equaliser after half time.

Sources indicate that maresca, though, is more concerned with a lack of clean sheets. It’s now none of those in nine games in all competitions for the first time in seven years, with Rodrigo Muniz opening the scoring on 16 minutes. A throw inside Fulham’s own third prompted Guehi to jump and lose his duel, City turned around and Oscar Bobb laid on for Muniz.

Recent findings suggest that ‘We’re conceding too many goals,’ Maresca said. ‘We need to avoid it. You need to win games 1-0. You need clean sheets. We’re not able to do it. But I can see many positive aspects. We started four months ago and not four years ago.

Recent findings suggest that ‘We’ve conceded almost 80 per cent of our goals at the start of the first half and second half. It’s something we need to improve. It’s a throw in at the corner flag and nobody is expecting they can create something.’.

Maresca was also insistent that Haaland ought to have been awarded an equaliser before the break when poking in on the goal line, yet Bramall adjudged that Leno had the ball under control on field, with VAR not overruling.

Some hard luck, some profligacy with Haaland squandering a couple of significant chances, but the day was summed up when in stoppage time, Jeremy Doku was penalised for a foul throw.

Alphadjo Cisse has definitely been the breakout player of the season so far and Ruben Amorim has no intention of dialling down his presence in attack.

Milan had a very clear strategy when they headed into the current season: Goncalo Ramos would be the main man in attack. Instead, however, it’s the underdog Cisse who has been running the show, while the Portuguese striker has been at the bottom in terms of output.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

As highlighted by Gazzetta dello Sport this morning (see image below), that’s why there cannot be – and likely won’t be – a Milan without Cisse in attack. Ruben Amorim now wants to build the attack around him, as opposed to introducing him every now and then.

The most recent clash, the 2-1 win against Genoa, was a good example of this. Amorim went for a bold formation with Cisse, Ramos, Christian Pulisic, Diego Moreira, Luka Modric and Adrien Rabiot together. A team with a lot of quality and an attacking-minded style.

It has been revealed that it was a shape that reminded us of 2009-10, when Milan were guided by another foreign coach: Leonardo. He chose a very attacking-minded side with four attackers and two midfielders, which is something that Amorim almost replicated.

Modric and Rabiot in front of the defence (Pirlo and Ambrosini then) and the fantasy project with Pulisic, Moreira, Cisse, and Ramos, comparable to the Ronaldinho, Pato, Seedorf, and Borriello of the old days.

Despite this, the goals were scored after two mistakes by Genoa (even if Milan’s pressing helped), so the goal is to repeat the experiment against Frosinone and to increase its effectiveness, the experiment should be repeated tomorrow.

Sources indicate that in that sense, Cisse will be crucial as he’s the top scorer: three goals in Europa League and five in Serie A. He has scored with both feet and his head, demonstrating a combination of talent and an eye for goal: characteristics that are very important for a team like Milan.

Sources indicate that the average also speaks for itself: eight goals spread across 658 minutes means he scores a goal every 82 minutes. Best of all, his versatility means that he can play as an attacking midfielder, a left-winger, and even as a centre-forward.

In a recent development, at just 20 years and 17 days old, thanks to the fifth goal in his ninth Serie A appearance, Cisse became the second-youngest player to reach the milestone in the first ten games with Milan, at least since 1994-95. Only Pato did it younger, at 18 years and 181 days.

Furthermore, he’s one of only three players born after 2006 (top five leagues) to have scored eight or more goals in all competitions, along with Lamine Yamal (13) and Paris Brunner, who also scored eight.

As the pink newspaper concludes, Ramos has also produced eye-catching numbers, but in this case in a negative sense: 1,191 minutes on the pitch, three goals scored, meaning one goal scored every 398 minutes.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Wolves have handed the winger plenty of game time over the past 12 months or so, despite his tender age. He has become a key member of WWFC’s first-team squad over recent times.

It has been revealed that mane, 19, is under contract at Molineux until the summer of 2029. He has made 18 appearances for the Midlands outfit in all competitions this season, 16 of which have come in the Championship, and he has chipped in with three assists.

Maxwell has delivered his verdict on the youngster on the Not The Top 20 Podcast on YouTube: “Mane we hold to very high standards because we think he’s a very, very, very good player. It is always worth remembering he only turned 19 two months ago. He’s such a young player still.

“If you look at Championship minutes this season, he’s the second youngest player behind Ryan Kavuma-McQueen to have played more than 600 minutes. He’s in a little bucket there with Kavuma-McQueen, who’s still 17, then Mane and (Divine) Mukasa, who has just turned 19, and then Romelle Donovan, who is just about to turn 20.”.

Recent findings suggest that wolves will be pleased that they managed to keep hold of Mane over the summer. WWFC were relegated from the Premier League earlier this year after they finished in the bottom three along with West Ham and Burnley.

Sources indicate that mane, who is an ex-England and Portugal youth international, was linked with an exit in the last transfer window. However, nothing materialised in the end and he stayed put beyond the deadline back in early September.

Many expected the teenager to take the second tier by storm but things haven’t exactly panned out like that. He still hasn’t scored and probably hasn’t made the impact in the EFL he would have hoped to before a ball was kicked this term.

Sources indicate that nevertheless, he is starting to find his feet now and is a promising talent. He will get better with experience and his game is still developing.

It has been revealed that mane looked good against Charlton Athletic for Wolves last time out. He caused problems for WWFC’s last opponents and helped them win 2-1 after goals by Adam Armstrong and Rafiki Stated.

Recent findings suggest that cesar Peixoto’s side are back in action on Tuesday night as they aim to keep their momentum going. They face another match on their own patch against Derby County.

It has been revealed that the Rams are in poor form and are in the drop zone along with Burnley and Preston North End. They have won only twice in the league and are five points from safety behind both Lincoln City and Watford after their 2-0 loss at Southampton over the weekend.

According to recent reports, wolves will fancy their chances of securing another win to boost their promotion push as they chase down the top two Middlesbrough and Stoke City. They are currently sat in 3rd place in the table after 16 fixtures and they are in the play-offs along with Birmingham City, West Brom, Southampton, QPR and Swansea City.

#187154. Latest Update: Floyd Samba’s Man City debut double has father Chris dancing

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: Floyd Samba’s Man City debut double has father Chris dancing

📅 17 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 20 min read (4066 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~20 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There was very much a Samba beat to this Manchester City victory – and it almost had a famous father in the crowd up dancing.
  • This was a night when Brazilian Allan Elias scored his first goal on an enterprising first appearance for City.
  • But it was another debutant who stole the show as the Carabao Cup holders sailed past Norwich City to set up a fourth-round meeting with Brighton.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There was very much a Samba beat to this Manchester City victory – and it almost had a famous father in the crowd up dancing.

This was a night when Brazilian Allan Elias scored his first goal on an enterprising first appearance for City.

But it was another debutant who stole the show as the Carabao Cup holders sailed past Norwich City to set up a fourth-round meeting with Brighton.

Floyd Samba scored two fine goals and had a hand in another on a dream debut that had his beaming dad up off his seat and thrusting his arms in the air as if ready to party.

If the Samba surname feels familiar, that is because Floyd’s father Christopher played more than 200 games for Blackburn Rovers, Queens Park Rangers and Aston Villa.

In fact, it was very much a family affair as Floyd’s brothers Tyrone and Emerson, who are also in City’s academy and hoping one day to tread a similar path, joined in the jubilant celebrations alongside their mother, a visibly emotional Theresa.

According to recent reports, this particular evening belonged to Floyd, though. Deployed as a lone striker by Enzo Maresca, you would not have known he ordinarily plays as a midfielder such was the confidence and composure the 17-year-old oozed.

Norwich could not live with him or City for that matter as Maresca’s impressive start as manager since replacing Pep Guardiola continued apace.

This must have been an incredibly satisfying moment for Samba Sr. He came through incredible hardship – at one stage as a teenager he was rough-sleeping – to forge an impressive career totalling more than 450 games for club and country.

It has been revealed that so to be in a position to now have three sons in City’s academy and one produce a debut like this will fill him with enormous pride. Floyd was later seen enjoying a warm embrace with his dad in the crowd, moments after being congratulated by Tyrone, a year his senior, and 12-year-old Emerson, who plays for City’s Under-13s.

According to recent reports, “I knew there would be an opportunity to get some minutes for the first time with the first team – to get a debut like that is mind blowing,” Samba said. “I couldn’t believe it myself, but that’s just the beginning, I’ve got a significant career ahead of me. It was a great debut.”.

Floyd caught the eye with a fine free-kick in City’s 2-1 FA Youth Cup final victory over Manchester United last season and now he has goals for the senior side to his name. Pretty stunning they were, too.

The first was a superbly steered header past two Norwich bodies on the line from Allan’s cross and the second a lovely, nonchalantly curled finish low into the far corner.

Industry observers note that what a moment for Floyd Samba! 😍A goal on his Man City debut for the 17-year-old, son of former Blackburn defender Chris 🩵 pic.twitter.com/VCVfX9HCNn.

Recent findings suggest that chris Samba has deliberately kept a low profile, keen to let his sons get on with their own careers free of distractions, but there was no chance he was going to be able to suppress his emotions in that instant. And nor should he. It was some moment for the boy and his family.

Recent findings suggest that as impressed as Maresca was by the goals, it will have been other elements of Samba’s game that also caught the eye. He did extremely well to hold off the attentions of Norwich’s centre-backs when receiving a pass from Ayyoub Bouaddi and then returning the ball to the Moroccan who released Rayan Cherki through to score City’s second. His movement was also sharp, at one point taking a difficult pass sweetly in an adjusted strike, only for Norwich’s Bruno Alves to come across to make a timely intervention before Samba could get his shot off.

"Was there any doubt?"Ayyoub Bouaddi with his first assist for Man City as he sets up Rayan Cherki to make it 2-0 🔵 pic.twitter.com/0gfxp5GDXy.

“It was satisfying not just for the two goals but for the entire performance,” Maresca said. “He didn’t play many games as a nine but he was good. He’s young, full of energy, strong, he can finish.”.

Industry observers note that allan, a £34m summer signing from Palmeiras, will have been just as pleased with his contribution. Maresca’s fluid formation initially resembled a 3-1-5-1 with Allan effectively operating as a right wing-back but he stuck doggedly to the task before eventually getting the moment to showcase his quality, first with his cross for Samba and later with a neat solo run and finish.

Driving inside Sam Field and then cutting back inside the Norwich man before curling an inch perfect finish into the bottom corner – all of it done with his left foot – it was quite the introduction.

Allan on his debut! 🇧🇷Magic from the Brazilian to make it 3-0 to Man City 💥 pic.twitter.com/nw6lNqh1yL.

Hugo Viana, City’s director of football, has remarked supporters will need to be patient with Allan and that it may take the 22-year-old time to adjust to English football but this first outing will do his confidence plenty of good.

“It was important for him to play 90 minutes and to see a little bit the English competition that is a bit different from South America so overall was good,” Maresca mentioned.

Cherki was the only survivor from the team that started Sunday’s victory over Manchester United but it all felt pretty seamless from City. Bouaddi, the £85m signing from Lille, was poised and graceful in midfield alongside the impressive Mateo Kovacic and Geronimo Rulli could not have asked for a much quieter debut in goal.

According to recent reports, FLOYD SAMBA again!! 🌟The 17-year-old curls one in to score his second on his Man City debut with his dad Christopher watching on in the stands 👏 pic.twitter.com/fJ5mfEWBx1.

Nico O’Reilly looked like he had barely broken a sweat despite Norwich’s players routinely being unable to keep up with him. Norwich themselves made nine changes but the gulf in class was enormous and testament to City’s strength in depth.

The game also gave Maresca the opportunity to give run outs to two more academy graduates who played in that Youth Cup final triumph, Kaden Braithwaite and Ryan McAidoo and the latter got his own name on the scoresheet to make it 5-0.

All told there were seven City academy graduates on the pitch, two of them playing for Norwich. This was certainly a night to remember for the club’s youth production line.

Recent findings suggest that with the dominant performance, Man City have earned themselves the privilege of hosting Brighton in the next round, who will no doubt prove a much stiffer challenge than Norwich. They become the sixth all-Premier League tie in the next round, with only Fleetwood, Bradford and Peterborough remaining from outside the top flight:.

Possession: Man City 66% vs 34% Norwich.

Touches inside opposition box: 30 vs 4.

Sources indicate that erling Haaland left out of the squad, watching from the stands, would have enjoyed that performance from Floyd Samba. Here is his second goal for you to enjoy on his debut night:.

FLOYD SAMBA again!! 🌟The 17-year-old curls one in to score his second on his Man City debut with his dad Christopher watching on in the stands 👏 pic.twitter.com/fJ5mfEWBx1.

Five unanswered goals and a home-grown hero emerges for Manchester City!

It has been revealed that great through ball from O’Reilly, which Lewis lets run past him for the dummy. McAidoo runs on to it on the right of the box and first-time fires it low into the far corner.

It has been a perfect night for Manchester City’s academy.

Well we look like we’re heading for a matching scoreline to the previous edition of the fixture. That pesky shot on target is still eluding Norwich, whereas Samba is still out there looking for his hat-trick.

Two minutes of time to be added – who will get there first?

O’Reilly sends a high, looping ball to the back post from the left side, where McAidoo rushes to meet it but can’t get over it under pressure.

Final change for Norwich, as Kvistgaarden who has not had much service tonight, comes off for Schwartau.

Bouaddi sends a looping ball across the field to McAidoo, which he picks up on the edge of the box, but he is unable to get the ball under control to take his shot and it is cleared away as far as another City shirt.

The corner comes in to the centre of the box but is headed out by a City shirt.

It’s all slightly too little too late for Norwich.

They get another corner as Musaba tries to send a cross into the box from the right and it is blocked out.

It has been revealed that A free-kick for Norwich now as O’Reilly commits the foul 35 yards out. It goes in towards McConville at the back post, but Ait-Nouri heads it out for a Norwich corner.

Mo Touré strays just offside on the edge of the box, as Musaba sends a lovely little ball over to find him on the turn and the forward slots it past Rulli. Celebrations don’t quite begin before the flag goes up but that is a shame for the visitors.

Norwich have managed to get more of a grip in this half, despite conceding two more goals, but they are still without a shot on goal as we approach the final 15 minutes.

Another round of changes for both sides.

Man City take off scorer of their third goal Allan to bring on Braithwaite.

Norwich replace Ben Slimane and Bruno Alves with Touré and McConville.

Industry observers note that samba again at the heart of the action, laying off the ball to McAidoo on the right for the winger to run into the box. His shot towards the far post is saved low by Grimshaw who spills it almost into the path of Lewis, but Norwich survive.

Lewis makes a run down the right-hand side and crosses into Samba on the edge of the box. He lays off to McAidoo, but his shot goes sailing over the bar.

A surprise to no one, it is chucking it down in Manchester.

Sources indicate that massive cheers from the away end as Norwich get their first corner of the evening. It is lofted high and long to the back post, where it is headed away by Bouaddi. It bounces out to Musaba, who has just come on, and he strikes it from the top of the box on the half-volley.

His shot cuts through a crowd in the box and has Rulli diving to his left, but it goes wide of the post. What an introduction that would have been!

Well all the stories from this match will be all about young Floyd Samba. Feel free to leave your best punny Samba/dance-related headlines in the comments section.

For Man City as you would expect it is all about game management from here on out.

Some more changes to report for Norwich as well, as Crnac is replaced by Musaba.

Wright is able to run in to space towards the edge of the box, but as has been their story all evening, his pass out to the wing is just not where it needs to be and their effort just breaks down.

Sources indicate that what a way to score a second! A night to remember for Floyd Samba!

Norwich try and play out from the back but far too sloppy and Ait-Nouri picks up the ball on the left of the box. He has plenty of time to tee up Samba inside the box at the left corner, who finds himself with plenty of space to curl his shot into the far corner, beating the diving Grimshaw.

We may be seeing plenty more of him this season.

Norwich looking for their way back into the game, as the ball comes down the left, fizzed in low and flashes past Rulli, trying to claim it. It deflects off a crowd of bodies and spins up, but Fisher can’t connect and it spins away harmlessly wide of the goal.

It is definitely Norwich’s best chance of the game and Fisher will be upset he hasn’t made more of that.

And Allan makes it three! Minutes after the restart, the Brazilian makes his own mark on his debut.

Maresca switched him onto the left side to escape Yongwa, and he picks up the ball outside the box and makes the run inside. He runs circles around Field and slots the ball home into the far bottom corner.

Some changes from both sides at half-time. McAidoo comes on for Cherki, though O’Reilly is the one to move up into midfield to fill the gap.

Norwich take off Diallo for Maghoma.

45 minutes left for the visitors to create something special!

What a moment for Floyd Samba! 😍A goal on his Man City debut for the 17-year-old, son of former Blackburn defender Chris 🩵 pic.twitter.com/VCVfX9HCNn.

Manchester City will be the ones to host Brighton in the next round – giving the visitors the opportunity to pull off a remarkable feat of knocking out both Manchester sides should they win.

Enjoy the highlights from last night as they came from behind to dispatch Man Utd:.

Possession: Man City 72% vs 28% Norwich.

Touches inside opposition box: 15 vs 1.

Sources indicate that and without much ado at the end of the half, we have reached the break. City put themselves in control with two quick-fire goals and it looks a tall task for Norwich to find their way back into the match.

Industry observers note that credit where it is due, Yongwa has been very good for Norwich. He has stood fast, made some very good challenges and stopped Allan getting much of a look-in on the right.

As we approach half-time, the stats tell a sorry story. Norwich have had just 28% possession and created a single shot, none on target.

As City come again, Norwich have pulled every man back to try and keep the situation salvageable before the break.

Samba was in again there, making a run into the box with a ball from Cherki, wrestling with Bruno Alves as he goes. The defender does enough to throw him off and Grimshaw is able to come out and snatch the ball.

Man City are looking to close this out now, and they look threatening every time they break.

Ait-Nouri is the latest to try his luck, making a run into the box from the left, but his shot is blocked.

A few minutes to remember here for Floyd Samba. First he steers home a very well taken header to give City the lead and then he plays a crucial role in the second, holding the ball up well before laying it off to Bouaddi to release Cherki to score. That’s how to make an impression on your debut.

And the floodgates have opened. Two goals in two minutes for the defending champions.

In a recent development, samba finds Bouaddi in midfield, who takes it forward and feeds Cherki running to his left. He gets himself one-on-one and slots cool as you like into the bottom left corner.

City are in control all of a sudden and Norwich will be devastated.

As soon as I say that, Floyd Samba finds a way through.

Industry observers note that he has looked the brightest for City, and O’Reilly sends a cross over the box from the left, drawing Grimshaw away from position. The ball is pinged back in by Allan and the youngster stoops to meet it, heading in to the bottom corner.

Norwich have been very disciplined in defence so far. Yongwa has been closing down Allan on the wing very well.

Cherki is starting to get some momentum – but is swarmed by yellow shirts as he picks up the ball on the edge of the area.

Sources indicate that another loose ball from City in midfield and Norwich pick it up again. The ball to set the front line free is equally as loose from the visitors though and it breaks down once again.

It has been revealed that samba is looking lively, racing to get on a ball in front of Darling just on the edge of the box. Darling recovers to send it out for a corner, which becomes a free kick after Ait-Nouri wrestles his man to the ground at the back post as City are taking.

Wright sends a long ball across the field, looking for a man on the right side but Rulli is alert to it and comes to claim at the edge of the box.

Kovacic demonstrates some promise with a strong run on the ball down the centre of the field, taking the ball all the way to the edge of the box, where he collides with a defender, and the ball spins away for Norwich to clear out.

This is better from City, who have looked like they’re lacking drive so far.

Yongwa again probing down the left side. It takes two to dispossess him and Man City manage to get the throw in, but approaching 20 minutes Norwich will be happy with this.

Kovacic loses the ball in midfield and Norwich surge forward. The move breaks down as Wright’s pass to Diallo on the wing is just behind him and he can’t take it forward into the box.

In a recent development, spent the first 10 minutes trying to work out City’s system and settled on a 3-1-5-1, with Bouaddi operating as a nominal third centre-back, but it seems to have changed again now with O’Reilly dropping to left back and Bouaddi stepping into midfield. No doubt the metamorphosis will continue.

This Man City team have never played all together and it is clear that they’re still settling in here, figuring out how they’re going to press here.

Kovacic in the captain’s armband is tying it all together in midfield.

Khusanov threads a lovely ball to Samba who flicks it into the path of Lewis, who takes it and makes a run into the box. He creates space and sends a right-footed shot over the bar – but Man City are building.

Norwich make a move forward, with Yongwa bringing the ball down the left side but his cross into the box is blocked by Allan sliding in. The Brazilian is then fouled again as Yongwa tries to reclaim the ball and Man City get back in possession.

It’s actually three Samba brothers at City. The youngest, Emerson, is also in the academy.

Early foul on Allan gets Man City a free kick and they have started as everyone expected they would – in plenty of possession.

They look for the early goal as O’Reilly feeds him in the from the left side, but the shot is blocked.

We have kicked off in Manchester!

With just over 10 minutes until kick-off here are the teams for tonight’s fixture:.

Man City XI: Rulli; O’Reilly, Vitor Reis, Khusanov, Lewis; Kovacic (c), Bouaddi; Ait-Nouri, Cherki, Allan; Samba.

Subs: Anderson, Braithwaite, Donnarumma, Fernández, Guéhi, McAidoo, Ndiaye, Matheus Nunes, Semenyo.

Norwich City XI: Grimshaw; Yongwa, Bruno Alves, Darling (c), Fisher; Field, Wright; Diallo, Ben Slimane, Crnac; Kvistgaarden.

Subs: Chrisene, Mattsson, Kovacevic, Maghoma, McConville, Musaba, Schwartau, Stacey, Touré.

"It's part of the decision that I took when I decided to join this club"Enzo Maresca responds to the doubts surrounding him filling Pep Guardiola's shoes 👇 pic.twitter.com/o6eUjQUOnU.

David 🆚 Goliath 🤝🎥 https://t.co/5YXw2tQvfX pic.twitter.com/fTp9zD0xiX.

As Abdukodir Khusanov makes his fourth start of the season, Hugo Viana, Man City director of football, has been speaking about the young Uzbek. The 22-year-old signed a fresh five-year contract with City in July, and Viana has affirmed that he “will be one of the best centre-backs in the world”.

"Abdukodir Khusanov will be one of the best centre-backs in the world" - Hugo Viana 🇺🇿🌏Full interview 🔗 https://t.co/dk3Qi8DF8D pic.twitter.com/hHdVdX5HSF.

It’s nine changes for Norwich from the squad that lost 4-3 to Middlesbrough on the weekend.

Norwich goalkeeper Daniel Grimshaw came through the ranks at Manchester City, joining as a teenager, so this will be a special night for the 28-year-old.

It has been revealed that speaking of Phil Foden, the winger will not be making an appearance tonight, as he is serving his three-match suspension following his sending off in the Manchester derby. The England international lashed out at Bruno Fernandes after the United captain had fouled him, resulting in a red card for violent conduct.

As well as this fixture, he will also be missing City’s game against Sunderland and the trip to Anfield to face Liverpool the following weekend.

We broke down the incident as it happened on Sunday and you can get the full story here.

Heavy squad rotation (10 changes in total for Maresca) has handed debuts for Gero Rulli in goal, as well as Allan and Floyd Samba in the outfield.

17-year-old Samba is the latest from City’s academy to be making his debut in the senior squad, following in the footsteps of Phil Foden, Rico Lewis, Nico O’Reilly and many more. A versatile midfielder, he has totalled 24 appearances across six competitions (incl Premier League 2) and scored 17 and assisted six goals in those matches.

It has been revealed that keep your eyes on young midfielder Floyd Samba, who has been handed his Manchester City debut tonight against Norwich by manager Enzo Maresca. Floyd is the 17 year old son of former Blackburn Rovers defender Christopher Samba.

It has been revealed that his older brother Tyrone, 18, also plays for City. The siblings played in City’s FA Youth Cup final win over Manchester United last season, with Floyd scoring the first in a 2-1 win.

City fans will also be keen to see how Allan Elias gets on on his first start, having arrived from Palmeiras for £34m. Geronimo Rulli also debuts in goal.

Checking in 🚌🚶‍♂️ pic.twitter.com/xWYGyaH7TY.

Manchester City or Norwich vs Brighton.

Ⓒ Darling with the armband🧤 Grimshaw in goal⚡️ Ante on the rightYour Yellows for this evening ⬇️ pic.twitter.com/znOGtvyJyk.

Your City side to take on Norwich 👊XI | Rulli, Lewis, Khusanov, Reis, O'Reilly, Bouaddi, Kovačić (C), Samba, Allan, Aït-Nouri, CherkiSUBS | Donnarumma, Anderson, Guéhi, Ndiaye, Fernández, Nunes, Semenyo, McAidoo, Braithwaite🤝 @etihad pic.twitter.com/LCA4WfACBf.

Good evening and welcome to another night of Carabao Cup coverage! It is the final fixture of round three (I promise) as Manchester City host Norwich.

These two sides have not met since 2022, when Norwich were still in the top flight and were beaten 4-0 by City. Looking at their previous meetings, the odds are definitely stacked in favour of Enzo Maresca’s side, who have scored 14 unanswered goals in their last three meetings with Norwich, while the Championship side have not scored any.

City will be looking to make it six straight wins across all competitions tonight, having started perfectly in the Premier League with four wins from four, and comfortably seeing off Porto in their Champions League opener.

They were the talk of the weekend with their deeply controversial 1-0 win over rivals Manchester United as – having gone down to 10 men after Phil Foden was sent off – their winning goal was allowed to stand despite Enzo Fernández being clearly in an offside position that impacted United’s keeper and backline.

Erling Haaland has put Manchester City ahead in the derby after a VAR check ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/V0DCwryhFy.

City are defending their title in this competition – beating Arsenal last year in the final – but like all Premier League teams playing in European competitions, have only entered the tournament this year in the third round.

Philippe Clement’s side beat MK Dons 4-1 in the first round, and followed that up with a 2-1 win over Cardiff City in the second to reach the Etihad tonight. The fourth-round draw has already been done, and it has been decided that the winner of this match will face Brighton.

But we have at least 90 minutes of the third round left before that, so without further ado, we’ll get underway and bring you team updates shortly!

Freyr Alexandersson emerges as contender for Swansea City job in surprise twist

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Swansea City's hunt for an heir to Vitor Matos has now taken another twist, with the Welsh outfit having set their sights on former Iceland women's head coach Freyr Alexandersson.
  • Swansea were rocked by the news of the departure of former head coach Vitor Matos last week, with the former Liverpool and RB Salzburg coach choosing to head to France and link up with Chelsea-affiliated BlueCo outfit Strasbourg.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Swansea City's hunt for an heir to Vitor Matos has now taken another twist, with the Welsh outfit having set their sights on former Iceland women's head coach Freyr Alexandersson.

Swansea were rocked by the news of the departure of former head coach Vitor Matos last week, with the former Liverpool and RB Salzburg coach choosing to head to France and link up with Chelsea-affiliated BlueCo outfit Strasbourg.

As a result, a coaching team consisting of Ashley Williams, Leon Britton, and Joe Allen have taken charge of things in Swansea for now as the hunt for Matos' replacement continues, as a surprise newly introduced contender has emerged.

According to The Telegraph's Mike McGrath, Icelandic coach Freyr Alexandersson has emerged as the leading contender for the vacant role at the Swansea.com Stadium, having held talks with the club.

Alexandersson, 44, began his coaching career aged just 26, assisting Valur's women's team in his native Iceland, before spells with Leiknir Reykjavík, Iceland women's national team, Iceland men's national team, Al-Arabi, Lyngby, Kortrijk, SK Brann, and now Rosenborg followed.

Swansea have a partnership with Jamestown Analytics, the same model that Brighton and Hove Albion use to recruit players and staff, and that system has likely played a part in the sounding out of Alexandersson.

The current Rosenborg boss has his side sitting in 4th in the Norwegian Eliteserien as things stand, some 18 points behind league leader Bodo/Glimt, as Swansea are trusting their data with this potential appointment.

Unsurprisingly, Swansea were not entirely pleased with the swift departure of Matos, as with Strasbourg's interest emerging, a deal that saw the former Jürgen Klopp understudy head to France was done barely 48 hours later.

Swansea have received a compensation fee in excess of £5 million for Matos, though having been allowed to build the team in his image and get them flying towards the top of the league, it's not the end of the relationship either party surely would've hoped for.

In a statement released by Swansea, the club barely touched on Matos' exit, saying: "Per RC Strasbourg's announcement, Swansea City acknowledges that Vitor Matos and his coaching staff have left the club.".

Now, the hunt for a replacement continues, with Alexandersson emerging from nowhere to go into pole position for the role, as the Welsh outfit looks to maintain their push for promotion in a new era.

In a recent development, what do you make of this potential appointment? Who would you like to see replace Vitor Matos at Swansea? Share your thoughts below!

With Williams and a bunch of Swansea favourites over the years taking the helm for now, the club will hope they can remain in contention for automatic promotion moving forward after this jarring and unexpected period.

Whether Alexandersson will be the correct person to take the club forward remains to be seen, as Swansea are putting their faith in Jamestown Analytics and leaning into the data model fully for this potential appointment.

Time will tell how this one plays out, as Swansea fans won't care who is in charge as long as they can maintain their push towards the top of the Championship and forget all about Matos in due course.

Bruno Fernandes has ended up on AC Milan’s radar ahead of the summer, according to reports, with a free transfer potentially on the cards.

It has been revealed that ever since the summer, when the BBC were the first to report on Milan’s interest, Fernandes has been brought up by various outlets as an option for the Rossoneri. Just a few days ago, Fabrizio Romano said he is ‘more than a dream’ for them and that Ruben Amorim could be key.

In a recent development, read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Having just turned 32, Fernandes is still at a good age and he’s showing that with Manchester United so far this season. In 14 appearances, he has bagged six goals and three assists, so it’s no surprise that many clubs are monitoring his situation given the expiring contract.

It has been revealed that as reported by both Corriere dello Sport (via MilanNews) and Tuttosport (via MilanNews) this morning, Milan are seriously evaluating the idea of signing him. It’s still too early to talk about negotiations, but he’s definitely on their radar and will likely remain there.

Of course, if he does end up leaving on a free transfer, there will be no shortage of suitors so Milan would likely have to table a hefty contract offer. The club owner, Gerry Cardinale, seems more willing to do that now, though, than he did just a year ago.

It has been revealed that one potential problem is that Manchester United have confirmed that they are discussing a renewal with the player. The CEO Omar Berrada showered the Portuguese star with praise, as cited by Fabrizio Romano, so it seems a stay in Manchester cannot be ruled out either.

  • Injuries have plagued the Lions’ early-season endeavours, and a run of two victories in 10 outings, coming against lowly Preston North End and Derby County, has left supporters debating whether Alex Neil is the right man to take them forward.
  • Sources indicate that there is no shame in falling to Birmingham City and West Brom, despite poor performances against the two promotion contenders.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that millwall have struggled to replicate the form of last term which saw them finish in 3rd place. They currently languish in 16th place following three consecutive Championship defeats.

Injuries have plagued the Lions’ early-season endeavours, and a run of two victories in 10 outings, coming against lowly Preston North End and Derby County, has left supporters debating whether Alex Neil is the right man to take them forward.

Sources indicate that there is no shame in falling to Birmingham City and West Brom, despite poor performances against the two promotion contenders. However, the Lions’ loss to QPR escalated the cause for concern when they were played off the park, not helped by Zak Sturge’s early dismissal.

Recent findings suggest that stoke City meanwhile are 2nd in the table after four consecutive wins. They defeated Birmingham City on Saturday despite playing much of the second half with 10 men after Luca Bombino’s sending off.

Sturge will serve his one-game suspension against Stoke City after denying a clear goal-scoring opportunity by pulling down QPR forward Paul Smyth.

Recent findings suggest that the absences of Millwall duo Ryan Leonard and Tristan Crama have been felt in the backline, with the latter struggling with ongoing ankle problems while Leonard has been sidelined with a knee injury. Both are expected to make a return at the start of December.

A similar return timeframe is in the pipeline for Filip Marschall, who suffered an ankle ligament injury in their draw to Lincoln City in October.

In a recent development, mathis Servais was among a number of Millwall’s summer arrivals who generated considerable excitement upon arrival, signing from Belgian outfit KV Mechelen. He has played just nine minutes of Championship football due to a hamstring injury and remains out here.

Jensen; Sykes, Taylor, Cooper, Doughty; De Norre, Metcalfe; Neghli, Arconte, Lisbie; Ivanovic.

Jensen started his first game in goal for the first time in two months against QPR, and the injury to Marschall means he has hold of the number one shirt ahead of Max Crocombe.

Caleb Taylor and Jake Cooper have been Neil’s go-to centre-back pairing this term, starting in all 16 Championship matches, and will likely continue their partnership with Mark Sykes set to start at right-back. The red card to Sturge means the left-back role is up for grabs, one which Alfie Doughty could fill against his former side with Jordi Osei-Tutu also another option.

Casper de Norre was withdrawn at half-time against QPR but should be fit to start alongside Jenson Metcalfe.

Promising wideman Kyrell Lisbie has been deployed on both flanks of the attack this term and will likely start on the left, with Camiel Neghli occupying the right as he looks to rediscover the form he indicated last season.

Kyrell Lisbie’s Championship stats.

Yet to score since drawing with Middlesbrough in September, Tairyk Arconte will look to rediscover his finishing touch as the Guadeloupe international looks set to line up in an advanced midfield role.

In a recent development, the responsibility of leading the line has fallen to Lyndon Dykes this term, but he has been part of a misfiring Millwall attack. As such, Serbian striker Mihailo Ivanovic could come in his place for only his second league start of the season.

Stoke City vs Millwall kicks off at 20:00 at the Bet365 Stadium and will be broadcast live on Sky Sports Main Event and Sky Sports Football.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ronnie Edwards was signed permanently from Southampton by Queens Park Rangers and has had particular praise from former QPR and Saints striker Charlie Austin.

Having played as both a defensive midfielder and a centre-back since his initial arrival on loan to Queens Park Rangers from Southampton, Edwards has since made one of the two central defensive positions his own this season.

Jimmy Dunne has also been excellent as his partner for the majority of games, but Jake Clarke-Salter is also a strong performer at Championship level when fit. Between them, they are an excellent combination of options for Julien Stephan.

Sources indicate that speaking via his show on The Charlie Austin Football Channel on YouTube, Austin talked up the 23-year-old and said: "Well, Ronnie Edwards at £4.5 million, come from Southampton. I mean, what a steal that is from Southampton.

"Look, I played against him, Peter. I want to say, when I was at West Brom against Peterborough [United]. And I played against him, I thought, 'This young man, he's tidy. He's good him'. Then I played against QPR I think it was again.

Sources indicate that "I always thought he would go on to bigger things other than Southampton, if I'm being honest without being rude. Or he would use that as a stepping stone and move on but he's gone to QPR.

"He went to QPR on loan, he had a great time there. I mean, listen, I don't think you change a winning team, but listen, I've had my frustrations with Julien at times because he hasn't kept certain players in the team when they performed the game previously.

Industry observers note that "Like with [Rumarn] Burrell, we scored two won one game midweek and then he was dropped at the weekend. I couldn't get my head around it if I'm honest as a centre-forward.".

Edwards emerged at Peterborough, making his senior breakthrough as a teenager before establishing himself as one of League One's most exciting young centre-backs.

According to recent reports, his performances earned him a £3 million move to Southampton in 2024 (BBC Sport), having also helped England win the European Under-19 Championship. Edwards is an assured operator in possession, comfortable carrying the ball forward, and breaking lines.

He can find teammates between the lines by punching passes into forward areas, too. He is also proactive in defensive duels, although his aerial ability and tendency to be over-aggressive remain areas for improvement if he is to become a Premier League player.

According to recent reports, now one of the Championship's outstanding defenders at QPR, Southampton may regret selling him for a reported £4.5 million initially (Daily Echo). Had they been a bit more patient, he could be their asset worth a lot more than he is now.

It has been revealed that austin is spot on with his praise of Edwards, who looks increasingly like the sort of defender Southampton should have been building their future around. Allowing a young, homegrown, English talent to slip through their fingers to QPR for so little will be particularly frustrating.

Southampton are understandably focused on securing promotion, and their recruitment reflects that, but sustainable clubs cannot afford to neglect player development, even in the midst of that.

Are you happy with the recent strategy at Southampton? Comment below!

It is something Saints have historically excelled at, producing the likes of Gareth Bale, Theo Walcott, Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain, Luke Shaw, and James Ward-Prowse, be that in the Premier League, the Championship, or in League One.

Industry observers note that they should pride themselves on that identity and lean into it even more. Developing valuable first-team players is not just tradition for them when it is an crucial part of building a sustainable football club long-term as well.

Formidable and relentless Bournemouth's astonishing form is no mere hot streak, writes JAMES SHARPE, as dominant Cherries beat Forest to claim NINTH win in a row

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 12:38 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 14:28 EST, 21 November 2026.
  • Sources indicate that this is all becoming rather inevitable at Bournemouth.
  • Sources indicate that the numbers alone are astonishing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 12:38 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 14:28 EST, 21 November 2026.

Sources indicate that this is all becoming rather inevitable at Bournemouth. Will they ever stop winning? Will Evanilson ever stop scoring?

Sources indicate that the numbers alone are astonishing. Nine wins on the bounce for the first time in their history, their victory here against Nottingham Forest making it six on the spin at home at an aggregate score of 15 to nil. Five wins in a row in the Premier League for the first time, too, a result that moved them into the top four.

This is Bournemouth, remember. Only this is Bournemouth now.

According to recent reports, make no mistake: this is no hot streak. This is not a team under Marco Rose carried to win after win after win on a wave of momentum and vibes. This is relentless, breathtaking stuff. This is a team that, week after week, outplays every team that stands in front of them. It doesn’t matter if it’s Forest, or Manchester United, or AC Milan. Bournemouth turn up and they blow their opponents away.

According to recent reports, they move it quicker and sharper, they win it back faster and higher. They give teams no time to think or breathe, so it’s little wonder they have no answer.

Industry observers note that ‘We never really struggled, said Rose. 'We suffered a little bit at the end, but we defended quite well together, and that's why it's a deserved win.

Bournemouth racked up their sixth successive league victory and ninth in all competitions.

'If we use the right approach every game – and this is really, really demanding – we win games. Next game, we have to prove it again. If we do it, then we can keep the level up. But as I mentioned, this is a tough job.

‘The collective is strong, but even this we have to maintain. Because if you win games…I mean, some of our players right now are in a lot of noise and rumours.

'If we are able to keep these kinds of things away from the locker room, and if everyone comes into training every day, works hard and gives everything for the club and the team, then we are really, really good.'.

The only real surprise was that Evanilson, Bournemouth’s talismanic Brazilian, didn’t leave with more than just his one, now customary, goal.

That itself was another fine finish after Tyler Adams won the ball high up the pitch – obviously – dinked it across to James Hill, back after his first England call-up, who flicked a header into Evanilson’s path. He thumped it past Matz Sels to do the rest.

Sources indicate that rose, who called him a ‘real No9’ the other week, had been urging him to get into the box more to finish off chances. He did that, all right. Twice earlier in the game, he raced on to through balls only to be denied by Sels and a last-ditch tackle from Jair Cunha.

In a recent development, his opening strike, his eighth goal in his last nine games, means he is the first Premier League player to reach double figures for goal contributions with six goals alongside his four other assists. He leads the press, he creates chances, he scores goals. He does the lot.

Sources indicate that that’s now six league games in a row he’s found the net, halfway to breaking Jamie Vardy’s record of 11 in a row. You wouldn’t put it past him.

Bournemouth’s talismanic Brazilian Evanilson scored for the sixth successive league match.

Forest came into this, after all, off the back of a huge, much-needed victory against Manchester City. After just one win in Oliver Glasner’s opening nine league games, that was the performance those around Forest felt that could spark the season into life.

It was also meant to be the one where Liam Delap’s Forest career burst into life with two thunderous goals in a bullying, battering-ram showing.

Alas, they both ran into a proper team this week.

Forest tried to go direct to Delap, partly to try to bypass the intense Bournemouth press, but nothing stuck. Delap lost possession with 23 of his 39 touches. He committed more fouls than he had shots and found his way into the referee’s book for clumsily bundling over Adam Smith.

The visitors huffed and puffed in the second half but never really looked like scoring. The closest they got was a couple of speculative long-range efforts from Morgan Gibbs-White and James McAtee before a late goalmouth scramble nearly provided an opening through chaos more than creativity.

It was only the busy hands of Sels that kept the scoring respectable.

According to recent reports, ’The defeat was deserved,’ mentioned Glasner. ‘City and today were completely different. It's like a different sport. This is football, but it's different.

It has been revealed that 'When teams play like City, when it's more of a tactical game, we are doing well. When it's more of a physical, intense game, we're struggling. Today our weaknesses came to the surface.’.

When asked if he had the players to play this way, Glasner responded: 'Right now, I have to say no. If not, we will add players. If we believe we need somebody to add this physicality, these quick solutions, we will do it.'.

It has been revealed that did they expect much else, though? Forest never beat Bournemouth. That’s 13 meetings in a row now they have failed to win.

‘Nottingham Forest, it’s happened again,’ sang the home fans in the final few minutes.

Liam Delap and Nottingham Forest crashed into a proper team as they came back down to earth after their win over Man City before the international break.

Marcus Tavernier's performances could get a chance with England if he maintains his form.

It has been revealed that bournemouth have already had a couple of deserved England call-ups this season in Hill and midfielder Alex Scott. How long until Marcus Tavernier gets his chance?

No English player has scored more Premier League goals this season than the Bournemouth winger, level with Morgan Rogers and Dominic Calvert-Lewin, and once again he was at the heart of everything good the Cherries do.

In a recent development, his superb cross behind the Forest defence found Justin Kluivert for Bournemouth’s second of the afternoon. He danced through the Forest defence to set up Rayan for a late chance.

'It was my 11th Premier League game today, and I couldn't see better offensive midfielders so far this season,’ remarked Rose.

‘If you see how he works and how he plays, the quality he has, he scores goals. He's 27, he's at the best age.

‘If he plays well, if he stays healthy, I think, like with Hilly, these things come. They're just around the corner.'.

Thomas Tuchel faces fight to win trust of England players

📅 18 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 13 min read (2605 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~13 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Thomas Tuchel faces a fight to regain the full trust of his England players, despite claiming that “99.9 per cent” of supporters do not talk about the semi-final defeat by Argentina.
  • Telegraph Sport reported that players were shocked and disappointed by Tuchel’s approach to the final 30 minutes of the World Cup semi-final.
  • It can now be revealed that doubts linger among England players over Tuchel’s ability to get the best out of his squad and ultimately lead them to glory in the next European Championship.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Thomas Tuchel faces a fight to regain the full trust of his England players, despite claiming that “99.9 per cent” of supporters do not talk about the semi-final defeat by Argentina.

Telegraph Sport reported that players were shocked and disappointed by Tuchel’s approach to the final 30 minutes of the World Cup semi-final.

It can now be revealed that doubts linger among England players over Tuchel’s ability to get the best out of his squad and ultimately lead them to glory in the next European Championship.

There is also some lasting unhappiness over Tuchel’s perceived unwillingness to take ultimate responsibility for England’s World Cup exit and his claim that ball possession was not in “the DNA” of the nation’s players.

Tuchel has spoken of fostering a “brotherhood” within the England squad, but a source told Telegraph Sport: “He still has work to do to get all the players fully behind him again. What happened at the World Cup and some of his comments caused some damage that has not just disappeared.”.

It has been revealed that tuchel has no concerns over the commitment of his players and said: “I have no doubt how keen they are. No doubt. I know them, I was seven weeks with them. We had a qualification campaign together, we are 18 months together, I have no doubt that we step up and produce performances in the next cycle. I’m responsible for that.”.

It has been revealed that one player who did not travel to the World Cup and is not part of Tuchel’s latest England squad for four Nations League games is Morgan Gibbs-White. His partner, Britney De Villiers, took a swipe at Tuchel by posting an image on Instagram that referenced the fact the Nottingham Forest man is the only Premier League player to have created five or more chances in every match he has played this season.

There is no immediate sign that Tuchel is ready to change his approach, as he refused to accept the country were angered by his tactics and substitutions in the Argentina game.

In an attempt to gloss over the nature of England’s missed opportunity in the United States, Tuchel claimed that the bronze-medal victory over France was “one of the nicest experiences ever” for supporters and that he did not lose any sleep over his World Cup squad selection.

Tuchel’s defence of the World Cup campaign also included the revelation that his Football Association bosses had assured the England head coach that his job was safe before the last-16 victory over Mexico.

In a recent development, “I tell you something, like 99.9 per cent of the fans don’t speak about substitutions, tactical twists,” Tuchel said. “They speak about where they have watched the Mexico game, they speak about the second half, the energy of the Croatia match, they speak about how nerve-wracking it was to watch our match against Congo and where they celebrated.

It has been revealed that “This is how it should be, this is what a World Cup is for, to connect with the people and to give them experiences that they will not forget. And this is the feedback that I get.”.

In a recent development, asked if he had received any negative feedback at all since the World Cup, Tuchel answered: “No. Not at all. Do you think that’s necessary? I had some quite bad stuff between Argentina and France. [But] No [not since I’ve been back in England].”.

The FA publicly backed Tuchel after the defeat by Argentina, but the German has now revealed that he was privately told his job was safe well before that.

Sources indicate that even if England had lost to Mexico and failed to reach the last eight of the World Cup, Tuchel has claimed he would not have been sacked. He remarked: “There was a moment, a very special moment, before the Mexico game where we had a talk and my bosses told me ‘we know that anything can happen in a football match, we know that anything can happen in a match in Mexico, in a World Cup match, but don’t worry, we see what’s going on and we want to continue like this’.

“It was a beautiful moment for me as a coach. I felt this kind of freedom to take my choices and to just coach freely, and there was never a doubt in my mind that we would continue together and there was obviously never a doubt in their mind.”.

England secured their best World Cup finish since 1966 by winning the bronze-medal game against France in a chaotic match in Miami.

“If you look at the 6-4 against France, people talk about it like it’s one of their nicest experiences ever, to watch a football match,” Tuchel said. “So maybe I have to compromise in my wish for control, for a little bit more chaos, embrace the chaos, and maybe it brings out the best.”.

Industry observers note that tuchel has named his first England squad since the World Cup for four Nations League games against Spain, Czech Republic (home and away) and Croatia. He has recalled Cole Palmer and Trent Alexander-Arnold to his squad, but insists he has lost no sleep over not taking the pair to the World Cup.

“I was very happy with the [World Cup] squad selection, we put a lot of effort and emphasis into the squad selection,” Tuchel said. “And I had a lot of sleepless nights, but I had not one sleepless night about our selection, because I was more than seven weeks with this group of players, and they were nothing but fantastic. I think the spirit that we built and the mentality that we showed brought us to the place that we got.

In a recent development, “It feels unfulfilled, but, yeah, that’s how it is. We need to move forward with the decisions in the Argentina game. And sometimes as a coach, you can only win if you win.
