Michael Skubala to Lincoln City prediction made as Bristol City pressure mounts

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • An intriguing prediction has been made on the immediate future of Michael Skubala as the 44-year-old's disappointing start to life as Bristol City head coach continued on Saturday.
  • The Robins were thrashed 5-0 by in-form Norwich City at Ashton Gate on November 7th, before suffering a 2-0 loss to Championship leaders, Middlesbrough.
  • Skubala was handed a three-year contract in the West Country in May after becoming the long-term successor to Roy Hodgson, who was drafted in as head coach in March following Gerhard Struber's somewhat controversial exit.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An intriguing prediction has been made on the immediate future of Michael Skubala as the 44-year-old's disappointing start to life as Bristol City head coach continued on Saturday.

The Robins were thrashed 5-0 by in-form Norwich City at Ashton Gate on November 7th, before suffering a 2-0 loss to Championship leaders, Middlesbrough.

Skubala was handed a three-year contract in the West Country in May after becoming the long-term successor to Roy Hodgson, who was drafted in as head coach in March following Gerhard Struber's somewhat controversial exit.

City have won just two of their last 11 Championship matches and have slumped to 18th in the table as a result, accumulating just 18 points.

With his side losing four of the last six games and conceding 12 times during that timeframe, supporters have begun to make their feelings known when it comes to Skubala's tactics.

However, circumstances at his former club, Lincoln City, don't appear to be particularly rosey despite the fact the Imps are residing outside the bottom three, which has caused an interesting debate between EFL pundits, Callum Fowler and Jimmy Smith on the Pyramid podcast.

Skubala has won just five of his first 17 matches in charge of Bristol City, culminating in a win ratio of just 29%, and his future is very much up for debate.

It was recently claimed by Alan Nixon that Ashton Gate chiefs have the money to end his three-year reign prematurely, and that background checks were being made on potential successors.

That is despite the fact Skubala believes he has retained the hierarchy's support, with CEO, Charlie Boss, revealing that a meeting had been held and that the head coach had been afforded the opportunity to turn the tide.

The length of stated opportunity remains unclear, but it has got off to the worst possible start despite the lofty position of Saturday's opponents, who netted through Adilson Malanda and David Strelec.

Skubala, of course, masterminded Lincoln's first return to the Championship since the 1960s last season as the Imps won League One at a 12-point canter, amassing 103 points and embarking on a 29-match unbeaten run.

Upon his departure to the Robins, Skubala issued a heartfelt message to supporters after 140 matches in charge, of which 71 ended in victory, but given Lincoln's four-game losing streak under joint-managers Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw, Fowler and Smith discussed the potential for the former head coach to return to the ProAmpac Stadium.

According to recent reports, "I mentioned it lots of times last season about Lincoln, it (Skubala's style) is disgusting," Fowler stated. "It's 'prison football', but in League One, that's class, and when you're someone like Lincoln, I guess that's class.

"For Bristol City who are a 'steady away' side anyway, with the money they've spent, you expect a bit more.".

When asked if Skubala could return to his former club, Fowler debated: "Would they want him?," to which Smith responded: "Yes. I think when a manager's won the league at a canter, you've got fond memories of him, haven't you.

"We look at Parkinson at Wrexham, and we think, 'what are they doing' if they want to kick on, but there's that connection.".

"Would the players buy into it if he went back," mentioned Fowler. "I definitely think it could happen, but I don't know if Lincoln are thinking about a sacking at the minute.".

Both then agreed that Skubala may lose his current role by the end of the three-game week.

We have already seen four managers sacked in this season's Championship, with three of the sides opting for a change in the dugout currently below Bristol City in the table, in the form of Burnley, Watford and Preston North End.

Skubala will have no doubt been grateful to have received the backing from the board during the international break, but defeat to Wrexham on Tuesday night would leave them even further adrift from where many expected the Robins to be under his guidance, which is to compete for a second play-off berth in three seasons.

Recent findings suggest that do you agree with this prediction on Michael Skubala's future? Comment below!

The Red Dragons had endured a slow start to the campaign themselves, but Parkinson's side have accumulated seven points from the last nine available, four of which came in encounters against Middlesbrough and Wolves, making City's task of achieving a vital win all the more difficult.

Patch on Watford’s pursuit of Edward Iordanescu as new boss talks stall

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, watford swiftly turned their attention to Edward Iordanescu after parting ways with Alessio Dionisi on Sunday.
  • In a recent development, yesterday, it was reported that Iordanescu had verbally agreed to become the new head coach at Vicarage Road, with the hope that he could take charge of Wednesday’s fixture against Blackburn Rovers.
  • The club remain hopeful of sealing the deal despite the setback.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, watford swiftly turned their attention to Edward Iordanescu after parting ways with Alessio Dionisi on Sunday. The Hornets sacked the Italian following a 4-0 defeat against Sheffield United.

In a recent development, yesterday, it was reported that Iordanescu had verbally agreed to become the new head coach at Vicarage Road, with the hope that he could take charge of Wednesday’s fixture against Blackburn Rovers. However, a new update from Sky Sports’ Anthony Joseph states that the Romanian is still in talks over his contract length and has not travelled to England yet.

The club remain hopeful of sealing the deal despite the setback. Iordanescu has been out of management since October 2025, when he departed Legia Warsaw.

He has mostly managed in his homeland, alongside spells in Poland and Bulgaria. A move to England would be the first in his career, should it be completed.

Watford have lost three of their last six matches, with their last defeat against Sheffield United. Although their defensive vulnerabilities stood out against the Blades, their attacking weaknesses have been more evident this season.

Clubs including Burnley, Bolton and Cardiff City have conceded more than Watford this season, while 16 teams have conceded less.

In a recent development, the Hornets are currently the lowest scorers in the Championship with 13 goals. Amin Nabizada is the club’s leading scorer with three goals, ahead of Myron Boadu on two. Furthermore, Watford have failed to score in seven matches so far this season. They also rank 19th in shots per match this season, highlighting the lack of creativity in the side.

Sources indicate that as a coach, Iordanescu’s philosophies place an emphasis on defensive organisation. This could help Watford, but they need to improve in the attacking department more.

The Romanian manager, should he join Watford, would bring international pedigree and trophies from his homeland.

However, Iordanescu has been at nine clubs in fifteen years, so he isn’t exactly a boss to build a long-term dynasty. He is yet to manage in England as well, which marks a risk in a likely Championship relegation fight.

Burnley opted for Fabio Celestini in their managerial search, another boss without English experience, and he is yet to turn his side’s form around.

Iordanescu would have the January transfer window around the corner to shape the squad to his liking. His impact will need to be immediate, as concerns grow at Vicarage Road.

Dave Challinor reveals how Barry Bannan can spend even longer at Sheffield Wednesday

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (936 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sheffield Wednesday boss Dave Challinor believes that Barry Bannan can "extend his career" if he deploys him in a deeper midfield role, but admits he is still experimenting with him across the midfield in the infancy of his time in the Hillsborough dugout.
  • The former Stockport County boss has had a very busy first couple of weeks at the helm in South Yorkshire, with games in three different competitions and a couple of big league outings.
  • In those two third-tier matches against Plymouth Argyle and Barnsley, Challinor chose the same starting eleven, which saw Bannan move further forward to partner Callum Slattery, creating two 10s behind Davis Keillor-Dunn.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sheffield Wednesday boss Dave Challinor believes that Barry Bannan can "extend his career" if he deploys him in a deeper midfield role, but admits he is still experimenting with him across the midfield in the infancy of his time in the Hillsborough dugout.

The former Stockport County boss has had a very busy first couple of weeks at the helm in South Yorkshire, with games in three different competitions and a couple of big league outings.

In those two third-tier matches against Plymouth Argyle and Barnsley, Challinor chose the same starting eleven, which saw Bannan move further forward to partner Callum Slattery, creating two 10s behind Davis Keillor-Dunn.

Against the Tykes, especially, he seemed to excel in that role, producing the kind of performance many expected Bannan to have already yielded this season. In truth, he's not been the Scotsman of old back at Hillsborough, but his free kick led to Jamal Lowe's opener, and he assisted the second, too.

That performance gives hope that the 36-year-old may still be key at this level, but Challinor feels that playing him further back could add years onto his career. Ultimately, it's a good conundrum to face.

Bannan indicated how he can still influence games further forward at Oakwell on Friday night, but the attacking midfield role will put more of a strain on what the veteran Scotsman can do, as it means he has to get up and down the pitch more often.

The Wednesday manager stated that, while his influence further forward could be useful, he could add one or two more years to his career by playing deeper and pulling the strings from there, something which Bannan has done throughout his time at Hillsborough.

"I think Barry can play in different roles,” Challinor stated, per the Star. "For how we want to play with control, him playing centrally and a tiny little bit deeper, because of his technical ability, I think will work really well.

"It will probably extend his career depending on how long he wants to play for because there'll be less demand on him to influence the game higher up, but he still has the ability to do that.".

Challinor admitted that it's a "luxury" to be able to have someone like Bannan who knows how to get into positions to influence games further forward, but knows that, right now, it's about experimenting with different players in different roles until Wednesday get to the January transfer window.

"I suppose the luxury we have at the minute is we're able to ask him to be a little bit more disciplined, but on other occasions let him go and be a little bit of a free spirit," he added.

In a recent development, "When he's higher up, he can certainly do that. He can roll into wide areas. He can come deep if he wants. But we have to find, let's say, different things at the minute because we don't have the players specifically fit in the positions that we'd like to have.".

Since Challinor came in to replace Henrik Pedersen earlier this month, he immediately changed the shape to a back three, similar to what he played while at Stockport in their back-to-back third-placed finishes in the last two seasons, before an injury crisis in defence forced him to a back four towards the end of last term.

Evidently, he's gone for formation over personnel, and is experimenting with what roles each player can play in this structure before the January transfer window opens, where it'd be expected that more players who fit this formation can be bought.

That's led to Jamal Lowe playing at left wing-back in the last two league games, but that's also partly down to both Max Lowe and Reece James being injured, and Bannan playing a bit further forward than he has been so far, given how he can influence games.

It may be the case that Challinor wants to see how Jaden Heskey can impact things in the meantime, or if he feels that the other options behind the striker aren't at the level of Bannan or aren't fit enough to play, so he feels he has to play him there for the time being.

Either way, it's a good question to have, and by January, we may see the Scotsman back in a deeper role.

Extending his career at Hillsborough should be on Bannan's mind, as the midfielder edges ever so closer to the appearance record for the famous South Yorkshire side.

The win over Barnsley was appearance number 496 in a Wednesday shirt, putting him eight away from tying Alan Finney for fourth all-time.

Andrew Wilson sits first on 546, but current club captain Liam Palmer is behind him on 524 and could likely break that record this season, barring any injuries or other forced absences, so Bannan may have to play a little longer to overtake his compatriot.

In a recent development, do you think Barry Bannan will end his career atop the all-time Sheffield Wednesday appearance charts? Let us know in the comments.

Sources indicate that the Scotsman turns 37 in a week, so he will need to be managed properly if he is to make Wednesday history before he retires. Playing him a little deeper and making him control the game without moving around too much could be the key to doing so.

Sources indicate that challinor got Oliver Norwood to play that role perfectly in his final two years at Stockport. Bannan may be a little older, but he still has the capabilities to do just that.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Charlie Austin compared the away dressing room at Millwall to a downstairs toilet due to how cramped it is.

The Den is widely regarded as one of the most intimidating stadiums in English football due to the atmosphere that the Millwall fans can generate, and it remains something of a throwback in the modern era.

Millwall supporters embrace that, and they pride themselves on how difficult they can make it for the opposition when they arrive in South Bermondsey.

However, it seems the club are also doing their part to make things tough for the away team, as Charlie Austin opened up on his experiences visiting The Den.

Speaking on the Chaz Kicks Off podcast, the ex-QPR striker discussed the different times he went to Millwall, as he also namechecked the players that could make it hostile, before sharing a light-hearted comparison of the state of the dressing room.

“I remember playing against Millwall for Swindon, when we got beat 3-2 on the final day. I was ****, and I was so nervous because I’d built it up in my head.

Recent findings suggest that “I went back there with Burnley, and we won 2-0, which wasn’t too bad. With QPR, we drew 2-2 and they scored right at the end, and I scored in the game.

In a recent development, “But, Danny Shittu, their centre-half, was as wide as the tunnel at Millwall, and he’s in there shouting, just trying to intimidate, so that’s when it starts. Then you had David Forde, the goalkeeper, he used to walk out last, which is unusual for a keeper, and he had a significant presence about him, where you’d think ‘I wouldn’t want to catch a right-hander off him’!

Recent findings suggest that “They don’t do anything in the dressing room, other than, the only way I can explain it - Millwall’s away dressing room is the equivalent of your downstairs toilet! It is small, and it is tight. It’s what you expect.”.

This is nice for Millwall fans to read, as every football fan wants their team to make their home ground a difficult one for opponents - and the Lions have managed that.

Clearly, things are different now, as you won’t get players like Shittu shouting in the tunnel to intimidate the away team, but it’s a good story showing how football used to be.

It’s fairly common for the away dressing room to be worse than the home one, and, again, it makes sense, as you want the away team to feel as uncomfortable as possible without crossing the line.

So, this is a good insight from Austin, and it highlights what clubs will do in order to try and gain even the smallest edge to help them on the day.

Whilst The Den understandably has a reputation, it’s fair to say it hasn’t been the fortress it once was so far this season.

That’s not to blame the fans, as they’ve made it raucous, and the 2-2 draw at home to West Ham produced a brilliant atmosphere.

It has been revealed that will Millwall make the play-offs this season? Let us know in the comments below.

Yet, for whatever reason, Millwall have been inconsistent on their own patch, and it’s a key reason as to why they’re not in the mix for a top eight finish at the moment.

But, there will be a belief among Neil and the players that they can turn things around, and picking up wins at home will be pivotal if they are to start climbing the table.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 15:17 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 15:31 EST, 21 November 2026.
  • Celtic manager Martin O’Neill hailed midfield duo Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain and Luke McCowan after the recalled pair both scored in the 4-1 home win over St Mirren.
  • With Mika Baur facing 10 weeks out with an ankle injury and Benjamin Nygren nursing a heel problem, O’Neill handed McCowan his second start of the season and Oxlade-Chamberlain his fifth, as the two joined forces for the first time.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 15:17 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 15:31 EST, 21 November 2026.

Celtic manager Martin O’Neill hailed midfield duo Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain and Luke McCowan after the recalled pair both scored in the 4-1 home win over St Mirren.

With Mika Baur facing 10 weeks out with an ankle injury and Benjamin Nygren nursing a heel problem, O’Neill handed McCowan his second start of the season and Oxlade-Chamberlain his fifth, as the two joined forces for the first time.

Oxlade-Chamberlain and McCowan netted either side of Camilo Duran in a nine-minute flurry of goals late in the first half with Callum McGregor making it four for Celtic in the second period before Killian Phillips reduced the deficit for Saints from the penalty spot.

Industry observers note that O’Neill noted: ‘Alex has been waiting around for a while to get into the side. He’s a brilliant passer of the ball. He took his goal very well with a calm finish in the bottom corner.

‘He was feeling a little bit sore, so taking him off was just precautionary.

Sources indicate that ‘I was also delighted Luke got his goal. That should give him a boost in confidence.’.

Oxlade-Chamberlain congratulates McCowan after he scored to make it three for Celtic.

McCowan faced criticism after Celtic’s Champions League collapse against LASK and his only previous start this season saw him taken off at half-time in a home defeat by Rangers.

O’Neill said: ‘I thought he did really well, also playing the full game given it has been some considerable time since he has done that.

‘He got the ball early on and played it almost blindly and it was intercepted and I thought, “oh, gosh, here we go”. But he roared back, took his goal well and I am really pleased for him. He is a real genuine lad.

‘It has been tough for him. In the game against Rangers, he was thrown into a position, and it didn’t start well for him in the match. I think he felt it was deja vu for him in terms of the game at the back end of last season too. That will be good for him.’.

The Celtic manager also introduced 19-year-old former PSV Eindhoven midfielder Joel van den Berg for a debut in the second half.

‘I thought he did very well,’ said O’Neill. ‘He’s coming on after an injury which kept him out for some time.

‘I am pleased there is a bit of competition for places now.’.

The veteran midfielder celebrates his strike that opened the scoring against St Mirren.

St Mirren manager Craig McLeish felt Celtic were clinical in his team’s heavy defeat in Glasgow.

‘It’s a really sore one with the way the scoreline ended up,’ mentioned McLeish.

‘I thought we started the game quite well and then that flurry of goals can happen here when you’re playing against such a strong team. The difference was the quality in our box compared to theirs.

‘They are just so clinical, and they get into those good areas and they punish you.

In a recent development, ‘I felt we got into some similar areas throughout the game. We didn’t give up, we didn’t move away from what we were trying to do, but we were just really lacking that final bit.’.

Key midfielder set for assessment as latest Blackburn Rovers injury enhancement emerges for Watford test

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that blackburn Rovers’ key midfielder Sam Morsy was absent from their 2-2 draw with Burnley after sustaining a knock in training.
  • It has been revealed that the experienced Egyptian has been an ever-present in Rovers’ side this term since signing in the summer.
  • In a recent development, meanwhile, Tom Atcheson is under concussion protocols after coming off early against Burnley, following a hit to the head.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that blackburn Rovers’ key midfielder Sam Morsy was absent from their 2-2 draw with Burnley after sustaining a knock in training. However, he is aiming to return to Championship action on Wednesday night against a managerless Watford.

It has been revealed that the experienced Egyptian has been an ever-present in Rovers’ side this term since signing in the summer. Morsy has featured on 14 occasions in the league, but is facing a race to be fit in time. On his fitness, caretaker boss Damien Johnson told the Lancashire Telegraph: “Sam was touch and go for the weekend and is similar. He is still being assessed this morning. We will have more news on that after training.”.

In a recent development, meanwhile, Tom Atcheson is under concussion protocols after coming off early against Burnley, following a hit to the head. The academy graduate has also been a regular feature with his impressive performances at the heart of defence seeing him keep his place in the Northern Ireland national team.

Blackburn Rovers have been spearheaded by the sensational form of Andri Gudjohnsen, who is only behind Will Lankshear in the goalscoring charts with 11 to his name. But, it has been a collective effort to see them sit in 13th place.

Rovers were showing signs of real promise prior to Tony Mowbray stepping away from the dugout, most notably an impressive 2-1 victory over West Ham before the international break, with Morsy and Atcheson firmly part of that.

Morsy has filled the role as the anchor of Rovers’ midfield admirably and has shown his worth as one of the Championship’s finest midfield operators at 35.

According to recent reports, atcheson meanwhile is at the opposite end of his career, but has been just as influential. He usually plays on the right-hand side of the back three and impresses with his desire to orchestrate attacks from deep.

Both Morsy and Atcheson are vital cogs in Blackburn’s machine and they will be desperate to have the pair available for a favourable-looking encounter against a troubled Watford side.

Hoping to close the gap to the play-off places to just two points with a victory, Blackburn will certainly fancy their chances with the opponents registering a solitary victory in their last five outings.

Morsy’s experience has been vital for midfield partner Kristi Montgomery who is enjoying his breakout campaign at Ewood Park, and his quality on the ball is still there for all to see at 36.

Nonetheless, Moussa Baradji stepped up to fill his shoes last time out, while Gady Beyuku also strengthened his case for a starting berth in place of Atcheson so Johnson has a wealth of options should either of his key players be unavailable.

Italy U21 coach discusses Cisse’s rise, next steps for Camarda and why Bartesaghi is ‘a luxury’

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (899 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sempremilan

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Italy’s U21 head coach, Silvio Baldini, has shared his thoughts on the Milan trio Alphadjo Cisse, Francesco Camarda and Davide Bartesaghi.
  • Industry observers note that in recent years, Milan have shifted more towards giving some of their academy graduates more playing time with the first team.
  • Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Italy’s U21 head coach, Silvio Baldini, has shared his thoughts on the Milan trio Alphadjo Cisse, Francesco Camarda and Davide Bartesaghi.

Industry observers note that in recent years, Milan have shifted more towards giving some of their academy graduates more playing time with the first team. Bartesaghi was the first to properly get in, cementing his spot in the starting eleven last season, while Cisse has been the massive breakthrough this season.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Camarda has had a tougher time after a loan spell at Lecce, but Milan have made it very clear through renewals and words that they will focus more on the youngsters. It’s exciting times as well, given how they have all performed with the U21 national team too.

Recent findings suggest that speaking to Gazzetta dello Sport this morning, Italy’s U21 coach Silvio Baldini was asked about the breakthrough of Cisse, Camarda’s current state of mind and why Bartesaghi is a ‘luxury’ for his team. Safe to say that he likes the trio a lot.

Cisse has had a proper breakthrough. Did you see that coming?

“Compared to a year ago, I can see a different guy, who’s more mature and prepared, with higher self-esteem, psychologically changed, simply stronger.

According to recent reports, “He has Milan to thank for signing him from Catanzaro in Serie B, believing in him and making room for him, then giving him consistent playing time. If he then makes the national team and does well, so much the better.”.

Milan deserve credit, and you also deserve credit for discovering him as a centre-forward….

In a recent development, “Analysing training sessions, a series of situations emerged where he managed to score by attacking space and depth: if you can do it on the right and left, it means you can also do it in the centre. But even there, the credit goes entirely to the staff.

According to recent reports, “They had the intuition, realising that Cisse could be useful to our game system in that way and at the same time, allowing Alpha to discover a new role successfully. I’m simply honest and meritocratic in my choices.

“Even though the goal against Armenia actually came from him as a second striker, at the end of that match we had two centre-forwards, him and Camarda.”.

Camarda, by the way, has struggled at Milan but scored for the U21s. How is that possible?

It has been revealed that “I can only speak about the work we do together. I spoke to him at length, I dedicated time to him, I asked him to explain his concerns, his fear of not being able to express himself as he would like. I told him stories of my own life, of how I came out of it.

“A dialogue not as a coach-player but as a son, or rather a grandson, as he could be, and a grandfather: from the heart. I’m not interested in performances as an end in themselves; they will come if he feels in the right place.

“I try to make him understand that I see him, I follow him in many small ways: he’s a conscientious boy who shouldn’t become obsessed with the goal, but rather experience football for what it is: fun.

“If, instead of fun, it becomes a test, then it worries you, and if you worry, you no longer enjoy it and it doesn’t help you perform at your best.”.

To have more fun, do you recommend that he should leave Milan for another team?

“I’m not going to get involved in this. There are clubs, agents, and a family: they know what the best path will be for him. Let’s remember that he’s 18 years old, he plays for AC Milan and in the Under-21s.

In a recent development, “It’s clear that the more he plays, the better it will be for AC Milan and for everyone. We’re talking about a great player, a champion in my opinion, who needs to finish his development: he’s still growing, he already has a great eye for goal, and he’s sacrificing himself for the team.”.

Camarda-Cisse: Can Milan provide the national team with one of the forward duos of the future?

“For me, yes. I see them as a permanent fixture in the national team, and of course they need to prove it and earn it on the pitch. But they have all the characteristics to do it. I found Alpha to be better prepared, even in his game decisions. Amorim did well to develop him.”.

The third Rossoneri player is Bartesaghi: more of a full-back like with you or a winger like at Milan?

“Davide is one of the best players in his position I’ve coached in many years. He’s talented, very professional, mature, introverted yet open, and that’s not a contradiction: he has enormous potential, and he indicates it every time he comes to us.

Sources indicate that “If I were any Serie A coach, I’d take him with me. For the Under-21s, Bartesaghi is a luxury. He plays with heart, passion, and intelligence, as well as possessing high-level technical, physical, and running skills.

“He can play in any position on the flank. In my opinion, if he starts 50 meters from the goal, he can perform at his best.”.

#187094. EFL club hit with unprecedented FA punishment – it's never happened before

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (358 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

EFL club hit with unprecedented FA punishment – it's never happened before

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (358 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Millwall have been handed a partial-stadium closure for their upcoming clash with Sheffield United in the EFL Championship, with the FA handing them an unprecedented punishment after ableist and homophobic chanting during their game with Charlton Athletic.
  • The chanting took place in the clash between Millwall and Charlton at the Den in January 2026 - a game that finished 4-0 to the Lions thanks to a late blitz of goals.
  • Official statements confirm that Millwall were in breach of FA Rule E21, which relates to a football club's responsibility to ensure its spectators and supporters (home and away) behave in an orderly fashion at matches.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Millwall have been handed a partial-stadium closure for their upcoming clash with Sheffield United in the EFL Championship, with the FA handing them an unprecedented punishment after ableist and homophobic chanting during their game with Charlton Athletic.

The chanting took place in the clash between Millwall and Charlton at the Den in January 2026 - a game that finished 4-0 to the Lions thanks to a late blitz of goals.

Official statements confirm that Millwall were in breach of FA Rule E21, which relates to a football club's responsibility to ensure its spectators and supporters (home and away) behave in an orderly fashion at matches.

Millwall have released a statement following the FA's punishment, where they have listed the sanctions they have faced for ableist and homophobic chanting towards Charlton.

Within that is confirmation that they have been handed a one-match partial stadium closure - the first time that an EFL club has been handed such a punishment from the FA.

The Athletic go on to confirm that it will be the Dockers Stand of the Den that will be impacted, with blocks 19, 20, 47 and 48 shut for the upcoming game against Sheffield United on December 8th.

That's going to impact a reported 1,274 fans who have tickets in that area, although they are invited to select an alternative seat in the stadium.

The additional one-match partial stadium closure that will be suspended until the end of next season will be activated if Millwall fans engage in more discriminatory chanting.

The statement from Millwall lays out what was chanted and why it was deemed unacceptable.

'South London S—' was the ableist chant, with 'You take it up the a—' the homophobic charge on the sanction.

Millwall's statement read: "Both chants are discriminatory and offensive, and the club condemns them in the strongest possible terms.

"Ableist and homophobic chanting, as well as any other form of discriminatory chanting, has no place in football or society. Any individual identified as engaging in such abuse will face the consequences.".

Millwall's next home game comes on November 28th when they host Burnley in the EFL Championship.
